```py
thread; an instance UFunction of the catalog runs on a live object of its
class (``call_found``), and outputs (``out``) are read from the parameter
block afterwards.

Mono compiles the method (see ``engine.prepare``), and a Frida interceptor on
its native code reports every call with its arguments, the calling method
and, if asked for, the return value.

Arguments are read where Mono's calling convention for the game's platform
puts them:

- x86-64 Linux (System V): ``this`` and integer-like values in rdi, rsi, rdx,
  rcx, r8, r9, floating point values in xmm0-xmm7, the rest on the stack. A
  struct larger than 16 bytes is returned through a hidden pointer argument.
  Where structs are passed by value depends on their fields, so arguments
  after a struct are not decoded.
- x64 Windows (Wine): rcx, rdx, r8, r9 or xmm0-xmm3 by position, the rest on
  the stack above 32 bytes of shadow space. Every argument, a struct too,
  takes one slot; a struct of other than 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes is returned
  through a hidden pointer.
- x86 Windows (32-bit Wine): everything on the stack, ``this`` first; 64-bit
  values take two slots, a struct its size rounded to 4 bytes. Every struct
  result goes through a hidden pointer. A float result is in the x87 register
  st0 and a 64-bit one in edx:eax; Frida reads neither, so they are not
  shown.

The hidden pointer comes after ``this``, or after a first reference argument.

When the game frees the memory of monitored code (Unity does so on exit,
when Mono releases its JIT code), the monitor is removed first: Frida would
otherwise write the original bytes back into unmapped memory when it is
unloaded, and abort the game. The agent watches unmapping for that
(``watchUnmaps``: ``munmap``, or ntdll's calls under Wine) and reports
``monitor-ended``.

The return value needs Frida to replace the return address of every call
with its own code. Mono cannot walk the stack through that code, so an
exception passing through the method can crash the game; hence it is
optional. With it, ``ref`` and ``out`` arguments are read again after the
call (``after``): an ``out`` argument only holds something then.

Arguments, ``this`` and results that are GameObjects or components show
their Unity name (``Health "Young Wolf"@0x…``): the monitor asks Unity for it
while the game thread is in the call. Names seen that way are also shown for
the same objects in snapshots and the inspector.

Values are ``{text, target?, snapshot?}``. ``target`` is an object, array or
struct the object inspector can open (``inspect``), ``snapshot`` its
contents at the time of the call (like ``inspect`` returns them, or
``{error}``) when the monitor records ``objects``. A string (not null) has
``string`` set; one longer than ``text`` shows has ``fullText`` (the id to
fetch it whole with ``full_text``; the agent keeps the texts of recent
calls) and ``length``.

Properties (parameterless getters, and a GameObject's components) are game
code that Unity only allows on its main thread. ``evaluate`` queues the call
until the main thread runs a script method (see ``engine.onMainThread``). The inspector
shows the current fields; a short-lived object may be collected by then.

Static methods can be called there too (``call``, see
hermes/features/method_call.py for the arguments).
"""

import itertools
import json
import queue
import threading

import frida
from PySide6.QtCore import QThread, Signal  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

from hermes.core import logs, messages
from hermes.core import sessions
from hermes.engines.registry import ENGINE_AGENT_SOURCE
from hermes.attach.frida_attach import CLEANUP_ERRORS, FRIDA_ERRORS, attach_session
from hermes.agent.source import load_agent_source


_AGENT_SOURCE = ENGINE_AGENT_SOURCE + load_agent_source(__file__)


def build_agent_source(language="en"):
    return f"const HERMES_LANGUAGE = {json.dumps(language)};\n" + _AGENT_SOURCE


class MethodMonitorWorker(QThread):
    """Keep a Frida session open and log the calls of monitored C# methods.

    The public methods are safe to call from the GUI thread; results come
    back through the signals.
    """

    # monitor id, {address, instance, params, returns, undecoded}
    monitor_added = Signal(int, object)
    # monitor id: the game freed the method's code (e.g. while exiting)
    monitor_ended = Signal(int)
    # request id, {name, address, fields: [{name, type, offset, static, value}],
    # properties: [{name, type, static, setter}], length?}
    inspected = Signal(int, object)
    inspect_failed = Signal(int, str)
    # request id, [{name, value}] of evaluated properties
    evaluated = Signal(int, object)
    evaluate_failed = Signal(int, str)
    # request id, [{name, method, owner, params, returns}] of an object's instance methods
    methods_listed = Signal(int, object)
    methods_failed = Signal(int, str)
    # request id, {params: [{name, type}], returns} of a static or instance method
    call_described = Signal(int, object)
    # request id, {result: value or None (void), outputs?: [{name, value}],
    # object?: value} or {exception: text}
    called = Signal(int, object)
    call_failed = Signal(int, str)
    # request id, the whole text of a long string value (None: no longer kept)
    text_fetched = Signal(int, object)
    text_failed = Signal(int, str)
    monitor_failed = Signal(int, str)
    # calls, dropped calls per monitor id, all calls per monitor id
    calls = Signal(object, object, object)
    worker_failed = Signal(str)

    _ids = itertools.count(1)
    _requests = itertools.count(1)

    def __init__(self, pid, parent=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.pid = pid
        self._commands = queue.Queue()
        self._ready = threading.Event()
        self._agent_error = None
        self._detach_reason = None

    def add_monitor(self, identity, returns=False, objects=False):
        """Queue a method (``CatalogMethod.identity()``) and return its monitor id.

        With ``returns`` the return value and what ``ref``/``out`` arguments
        hold afterwards are logged too; with ``objects`` the fields of object
        arguments (``snapshot``). ``None`` enables an option if the method
        has a result or objects; monitor_added tells (``recordsResults``,
        ``recordsObjects``, ``hasResults``, ``hasObjects``).
        """
        monitor_id = next(self._ids)
        self._commands.put(("add", monitor_id,
                            {"identity": identity, "returns": returns, "objects": objects}))
        return monitor_id

    def inspect(self, target):
        """Read an object (a value's ``target``); expect inspected or inspect_failed."""
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("inspect", request_id, target))
        return request_id

    def evaluate(self, target, names):
        """Call the named getters of an object on the game's main thread.

        Expect evaluated or evaluate_failed. Getters are game code: they may
        have side effects.
        """
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("evaluate", request_id, (target, list(names))))
        return request_id

    def describe_call(self, identity, instance=False):
        """Read the parameters of a static method, or with ``instance`` of an
        instance method (see ``call_found``); expect call_described or call_failed."""
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("describe", request_id, (identity, instance)))
        return request_id

    def call(self, identity, arguments):
        """Call a static method on the game's main thread; expect called or call_failed.

        ``arguments`` as ``parse_argument`` (hermes/features/method_call.py)
        returns them. Game code: it changes the game like the game itself would.
        """
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("call", request_id, (identity, list(arguments))))
        return request_id

    def call_found(self, identity, class_name, object_text, arguments):
        """Call an instance method on a live object of ``class_name``, on the
        game's main thread: the first one found if ``object_text`` is empty,
        else the one of that name or at that address (0x…). Expect called
        (with ``object``, the object it ran on) or call_failed. As ``call``: game code.
        """
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("call_found", request_id,
                            (identity, class_name, object_text, list(arguments))))
        return request_id

    def list_methods(self, target):
        """List the instance methods of an object; expect methods_listed or methods_failed."""
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("methods", request_id, target))
        return request_id

    def describe_method(self, method):
        """Read the parameters of an instance method (a ``list_methods`` entry's
        ``method``); expect call_described or call_failed."""
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("describe_method", request_id, method))
        return request_id

    def call_on(self, target, method, arguments):
        """Call an instance method on an object, on the game's main thread;
        expect called or call_failed. As ``call``: game code."""
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("call_on", request_id, (target, method, list(arguments))))
        return request_id

    def full_text(self, text_id):
        """Fetch the whole text of a long string value (its ``fullText``).

        Expect text_fetched or text_failed. The agent keeps the texts of
        recent calls only.
        """
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("text", request_id, text_id))
        return request_id

    def remove_monitor(self, monitor_id):
        self._commands.put(("remove", monitor_id, None))

    @sessions.tracked(sessions.MONITOR)
    def run(self):
        session = None
        script = None
        try:
            session = attach_session(self.pid)
            sessions.SESSIONS.set_frida_session(self, session)
            session.on("detached", self._on_detached)
            script = session.create_script(build_agent_source())
            script.on("message", self._on_message)
            script.load()
            if not self._ready.wait(5):
                raise messages.LocalizedRuntimeError("error.method_monitor.load_timeout")
            while (not self.isInterruptionRequested() and self._detach_reason is None
                   and self._agent_error is None):
                try:
                    action, monitor_id, argument = self._commands.get(timeout=0.05)
                except queue.Empty:
                    continue
                self._execute(script.exports_sync, action, monitor_id, argument)
            if self._agent_error and not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                raise RuntimeError(self._agent_error)
            if self._detach_reason and not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                raise messages.LocalizedRuntimeError("error.agent.detached",
                                                     reason=self._detach_reason)
        except FRIDA_ERRORS + (OSError, RuntimeError) as error:
            if not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                self.worker_failed.emit(messages.describe(error))
        finally:
            if script is not None:
                try:
                    script.exports_sync.dispose()
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)
                try:
                    script.unload()
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)
            if session is not None:
                try:
                    session.detach()
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)

    def _execute(self, api, action, monitor_id, argument):
        try:
            if action == "add":
                self.monitor_added.emit(
                    monitor_id, api.add_monitor({"id": monitor_id, **argument})
                )
            elif action == "remove":
                api.remove_monitor(monitor_id)
            elif action == "inspect":
                try:
                    self.inspected.emit(monitor_id, api.inspect(argument))
                except frida.RPCException as error:
                    self.inspect_failed.emit(monitor_id, messages.describe(error))
            elif action == "evaluate":
                try:
                    self.evaluated.emit(monitor_id, api.evaluate(*argument))
                except frida.RPCException as error:
                    self.evaluate_failed.emit(monitor_id, messages.describe(error))
            elif action == "describe":
                try:
                    self.call_described.emit(monitor_id, api.describe_call(*argument))
                except frida.RPCException as error:
                    self.call_failed.emit(monitor_id, messages.describe(error))
            elif action == "call":
                try:
                    self.called.emit(monitor_id, api.call_static(*argument))
                except frida.RPCException as error:
                    self.call_failed.emit(monitor_id, messages.describe(error))
            elif action == "call_found":
                try:
                    self.called.emit(monitor_id, api.call_found(*argument))
                except frida.RPCException as error:
                    self.call_failed.emit(monitor_id, messages.describe(error))
            elif action == "methods":
                try:
                    self.methods_listed.emit(monitor_id, api.list_methods(argument))
                except frida.RPCException as error:
                    self.methods_failed.emit(monitor_id, messages.describe(error))
            elif action == "describe_method":
                try:
                    self.call_described.emit(monitor_id, api.describe_method(argument))
                except frida.RPCException as error:
                    self.call_failed.emit(monitor_id, messages.describe(error))
            elif action == "call_on":
                try:
                    self.called.emit(monitor_id, api.call_on(*argument))
                except frida.RPCException as error:
                    self.call_failed.emit(monitor_id, messages.describe(error))
            elif action == "text":
                try:
                    self.text_fetched.emit(monitor_id, api.full_text(argument))
                except frida.RPCException as error:
                    self.text_failed.emit(monitor_id, messages.describe(error))
        except frida.RPCException as error:
            self.monitor_failed.emit(monitor_id, messages.describe(error))

    def _on_message(self, message, _data):
        if message.get("type") == "error":
            self._agent_error = messages.describe(
                message.get("stack", messages.text("error.method_monitor.agent_failed")))
            self._ready.set()
            return
        payload = message.get("payload", {})
        kind = payload.get("kind")
        if kind == "ready":
            self._ready.set()
        elif kind == "calls":
            self.calls.emit(
                payload.get("events", []),
                {int(key): value for key, value in payload.get("dropped", {}).items()},
                {int(key): value for key, value in payload.get("counts", {}).items()},
            )
        elif kind == "monitor-ended":
            self.monitor_ended.emit(payload.get("monitorId", 0))
        elif kind == "agent-error":
            logs.log.error("method monitor agent: %s", messages.describe(payload.get("error", "")))
        elif kind == "monitor-error":
            self.monitor_failed.emit(payload.get("monitorId", 0),
                                     messages.describe(payload.get("error", "")))

    def _on_detached(self, reason, _crash):
        self._detach_reason = reason

```

`hermes/features/native_monitor.js`:

```js
const MAX_LOGGED_PER_SECOND = MAX_LOGGED_VALUE;
const MAX_CHANGES = MAX_CHANGES_VALUE;
const MAX_STRING = 80;
const SYMBOL_BUDGET_MS = 200;
const WINDOWS = Process.platform === 'windows';
const MIN_POINTER = ptr('0x10000');
const MAX_POINTER = ptr('0x800000000000');
const PAGE = Process.pageSize;
// Frida replaces up to 14 bytes, and the rest of the instructions they cut
// into, with a jump: a hook within that of another one would patch into it.
const REDIRECT_SIZE = 14;
const REGISTERS = Process.arch === 'x64'
  ? ['rax', 'rbx', 'rcx', 'rdx', 'rsi', 'rdi', 'rbp', 'rsp',
     'r8', 'r9', 'r10', 'r11', 'r12', 'r13', 'r14', 'r15']
  : ['eax', 'ebx', 'ecx', 'edx', 'esi', 'edi', 'ebp', 'esp'];

const monitors = new Map();   // id -> monitor
let pending = [];
let modules = new ModuleMap();
const symbols = new Map();    // address text -> symbol text ('' for none)
let reportedCalls = -1;       // calls of all monitors at the last flush

function isPointer(value) {
  return value.compare(MIN_POINTER) >= 0 && value.compare(MAX_POINTER) < 0;
}

function readRegion(address, size) {
  // Up to ``size`` bytes, or up to the end of the page if the next one is not readable.
  try {
    return address.readByteArray(size);
  } catch (_error) {
    // fall through
  }
  const toPageEnd = PAGE - address.and(PAGE - 1).toInt32();
  if (toPageEnd >= size)
    return null;
  try {
    return address.readByteArray(toPageEnd);
  } catch (_error) {
    return null;
  }
}

function asciiText(bytes) {
  // The bytes as text if they start with a printable, NUL-terminated string.
  const view = new Uint8Array(bytes);
  let text = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(view.length, MAX_STRING); i++) {
    const byte = view[i];
    if (byte === 0)
      return text.length >= 3 ? text : null;
    if (byte < 0x20 || byte > 0x7e)
      return null;
    text += String.fromCharCode(byte);
  }
  return text.length >= 3 ? text + '…' : null;
}

function hex(view, start, end) {
  let text = '';
  for (let i = start; i < end; i++)
    text += (view[i] < 16 ? '0' : '') + view[i].toString(16);
  return text;
}

function changes(call, found) {
  // Ranges of changed bytes in the regions the arguments pointed to.
  const seen = new Set();
  call.regions.forEach((before, index) => {
    if (before === null)
      return;
    const base = call.values[index];
    let after;
    try {
      after = base.readByteArray(before.byteLength);
    } catch (_error) {
      return;
    }
    const old = new Uint8Array(before);
    const now = new Uint8Array(after);
    let i = 0;
    while (i < old.length) {
      if (old[i] === now[i]) {
        i++;
        continue;
      }
      let end = i + 1;
      while (end < old.length && old[end] !== now[end])
        end++;
      const address = base.add(i).toString();
      if (!seen.has(address)) {
        seen.add(address);
        if (found.list.length < MAX_CHANGES)
          found.list.push({ arg: index, offset: i, address,
                            before: hex(old, i, end), after: hex(now, i, end) });
        else
          found.more = true;
      }
      i = end;
    }
  });
}

function where(address) {
  // module+0x… of an address in a module, or ''.
  const module = modules.find(address);
  if (module === null)
    return '';
  return `${module.name}+0x${address.sub(module.base).toString(16)}`;
}

function symbolOf(addressText, deadline) {
  // name+0x… of the function an address lies in, or '' (not under Windows: dbghelp under Wine).
  if (symbols.has(addressText))
    return symbols.get(addressText);
  if (WINDOWS || Date.now() > deadline)
    return '';
  let text = '';
  try {
    // Frida names an address inside a function "name+0x…", one without a symbol "0x…".
    const symbol = DebugSymbol.fromAddress(ptr(addressText));
    if (symbol.name !== null && !symbol.name.startsWith('0x'))
      text = symbol.name;
  } catch (_error) {
    // unnamed
  }
  symbols.set(addressText, text);
  return text;
}

function value(pointer, region) {
  const text = region !== null && region !== undefined ? asciiText(region) : null;
  return { value: pointer.toString(), text };
}

function admit(monitor) {
  // Whether to log this call (else it is only counted).
  monitor.calls++;
  const now = Date.now();
  if (now - monitor.second >= 1000) {
    monitor.second = now;
    monitor.logged = 0;
  }
  if (monitor.logged >= MAX_LOGGED_PER_SECOND) {
    monitor.skipped++;
    return false;
  }
  monitor.logged++;
  return true;
}

function probe(monitor) {
  // A function as callback: an instruction probe, which leaves the stack alone.
  return Interceptor.attach(monitor.address, function () {
    if (!admit(monitor))
      return;
    const context = this.context;
    pending.push({
      monitorId: monitor.id,
      time: Date.now(),
      thread: this.threadId,
      registers: REGISTERS.map(name => {
        const register = ptr(context[name].toString());
        return [name, value(register, isPointer(register)
          ? readRegion(register, MAX_STRING + 1) : null)];
      })
    });
  });
}

function attach(monitor) {
  return Interceptor.attach(monitor.address, {
    onEnter(args) {
      if (!admit(monitor)) {
        this.call = null;
        return;
      }
      const now = Date.now();
      const values = [];
      const regions = [];
      for (let i = 0; i < monitor.args; i++) {
        const argument = args[i];
        values.push(argument);
        regions.push(monitor.dump > 0 && isPointer(argument)
          ? readRegion(argument, monitor.dump) : null);
      }
      this.call = { values, regions, time: now, thread: this.threadId, depth: this.depth,
                    caller: this.returnAddress };
    },
    onLeave(retval) {
      const call = this.call;
      if (call === null || call === undefined)
        return;
      const found = { list: [], more: false };
      changes(call, found);
      const result = ptr(retval.toString());
      pending.push({
        monitorId: monitor.id,
        time: call.time,
        thread: call.thread,
        depth: call.depth,
        args: call.values.map((argument, i) => value(argument, call.regions[i])),
        result: value(result, isPointer(result) ? readRegion(result, MAX_STRING + 1) : null),
        caller: call.caller.toString(),
        changes: found.list,
        moreChanges: found.more
      });
    }
  });
}

function describe(call, deadline) {
  if (call.registers !== undefined) {
    for (const [_name, register] of call.registers)
      register.where = where(ptr(register.value));
    return;
  }
  for (const argument of call.args)
    argument.where = where(ptr(argument.value));
  call.result.where = where(ptr(call.result.value));
  call.callerWhere = where(ptr(call.caller));
  call.callerSymbol = symbolOf(call.caller, deadline);
}

function flush() {
  let total = 0;
  for (const monitor of monitors.values())
    total += monitor.calls;
  if (pending.length === 0 && total === reportedCalls)
    return;
  reportedCalls = total;
  const calls = pending;
  pending = [];
  const deadline = Date.now() + SYMBOL_BUDGET_MS;
  for (const call of calls)
    describe(call, deadline);
  const counts = {};
  for (const monitor of monitors.values())
    counts[monitor.id] = { calls: monitor.calls, skipped: monitor.skipped };
  send({ kind: 'calls', calls, counts });
}

function resolve(spec) {
  // spec: {address} | {module, offset} | {name}
  if (spec.address !== undefined)
    return ptr(spec.address);
  if (spec.module !== undefined)
    return Process.getModuleByName(spec.module).base.add(spec.offset);
  if (!WINDOWS) {
    try {
      return DebugSymbol.getFunctionByName(spec.name);
    } catch (_error) {
      // not in the symbol tables: maybe an export
    }
  }
  const exported = Module.findGlobalExportByName(spec.name);
  if (exported === null)
    throw hermesError('error.native_monitor.no_function', { name: spec.name });
  return exported;
}

function patchSpan(address) {
  // The bytes Frida may replace with its jump: whole instructions, REDIRECT_SIZE at least.
  let size = 0;
  let at = address;
  try {
    while (size < REDIRECT_SIZE) {
      const instruction = Instruction.parse(at);
      size += instruction.size;
      at = instruction.next;
    }
  } catch (_error) {
    return Math.max(size, REDIRECT_SIZE);
  }
  return size;
}

function enclosing(address) {
  // {start, name} of the function an address lies in, by its symbol, or null.
  const text = symbolOf(address.toString(), Date.now() + 2000);
  if (text === '')
    return null;
  const inside = /^(.+)\+0x([0-9a-f]+)$/.exec(text);
  if (inside === null)
    return { start: address, name: text };
  return { start: address.sub(parseInt(inside[2], 16)), name: inside[1] };
}

function add(spec) {
  // spec: where (see resolve), id, kind, args, dump
  if (monitors.has(spec.id))
    throw hermesError('error.native_monitor.exists', { id: spec.id });
  const address = resolve(spec);
  const span = patchSpan(address);
  for (const other of monitors.values()) {
    const overlap = address.compare(other.address.add(other.span)) < 0
      && other.address.compare(address.add(span)) < 0;
    if (overlap && !other.address.equals(address))
      throw hermesError('error.native_monitor.too_close', { address, other: other.address });
  }
  if (modules.find(address) === null)
    modules.update();  // loaded since
  const inside = enclosing(address);
  let kind = spec.kind;
  if (kind === 'auto')
    kind = inside !== null && inside.start.equals(address) ? 'function' : 'instruction';
  const monitor = {
    id: spec.id, address, span, args: spec.args, dump: spec.dump,
    calls: 0, skipped: 0, second: 0, logged: 0, listener: null
  };
  monitor.listener = kind === 'function' ? attach(monitor) : probe(monitor);
  monitors.set(spec.id, monitor);
  const addressText = address.toString();
  const answer = { address: addressText, where: where(address), kind,
                   symbol: symbolOf(addressText, Date.now() + 2000) };
  if (kind === 'instruction' && inside !== null && !inside.start.equals(address)) {
    answer.function = inside.start.toString();
    answer.functionName = inside.name;
  }
  return answer;
}

function remove(id) {
  const monitor = monitors.get(id);
  if (monitor === undefined)
    return false;
  monitors.delete(id);
  monitor.listener.detach();
  return true;
}

const flushTimer = setInterval(flush, 100);
send({ kind: 'ready', platform: Process.platform, arch: Process.arch });

rpc.exports = {
  add,
  remove,
  dispose() {
    clearInterval(flushTimer);
    for (const id of Array.from(monitors.keys()))
      remove(id);
    Interceptor.flush();
    return true;
  }
};

```

`hermes/features/native_monitor.py`:

```py
"""Native function monitor: the calls of a function of the game's machine code.

The native counterpart of the method monitor (monitor.py), for functions the
native trace found or that are known by address or symbol. A Frida
interceptor on the function's first instruction reports every call with

- its first arguments, as the platform's calling convention passes them
  (x86-64 Linux: rdi, rsi, rdx, rcx, r8, r9; Windows/Wine: rcx, rdx, r8, r9,
  then the stack). Floating point arguments (xmm registers) are not seen;
- the return value (rax);
- the caller (the return address);
- what changed in memory: for every argument that points to readable
  memory, ``dump`` bytes there are copied when the call begins and compared
  when it returns. For a method of a C++ object the first argument is
  ``this``, so the comparison shows which fields of the object it set.

Changes elsewhere (globals, objects reached through pointers) are not seen.
A copy taken while another thread writes there shows that thread's writes
too.

Calls to a function the game makes very often are only counted beyond
``MAX_LOGGED_PER_SECOND`` per second, to keep the game playable.

All of that holds only at the first instruction of a function: to see the
call return, Frida replaces the return address on top of the stack. Inside a
function the top of the stack is some local variable, which that would
overwrite. An address inside a function (e.g. the instruction a write watch
reported) is therefore monitored as an *instruction*: a probe that sees every
pass with all general purpose registers, and touches nothing. ``kind`` tells
which: ``"function"``, ``"instruction"``, or ``"auto"`` (a function where a
symbol starts exactly there, else an instruction). Its answer names the
function an instruction lies in, if a symbol tells, to monitor that instead.

Frida replaces the first instructions at a hooked address with a jump. A
second hook a few bytes further would patch into that jump and crash the
game: the agent refuses hooks whose patched bytes would overlap.
"""

import re

import frida
from PySide6.QtCore import Signal  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

from hermes.core import messages, sessions
from hermes.features.trace import AgentWorker
from hermes.agent.source import MESSAGES_SOURCE, load_agent_source


# Calls logged per function and second; the others are only counted.
MAX_LOGGED_PER_SECOND = 200
# Changed ranges reported per call (a constructor changes everything).
MAX_CHANGES = 64
# Default number of arguments and bytes compared per pointer argument.
DEFAULT_ARGUMENTS = 4
DEFAULT_DUMP = 0x200
MAX_DUMP = 0x10000

FUNCTION, INSTRUCTION, AUTO = "function", "instruction", "auto"

_AGENT_SOURCE = MESSAGES_SOURCE + (
    load_agent_source(__file__)
    .replace("MAX_LOGGED_VALUE", str(MAX_LOGGED_PER_SECOND))
    .replace("MAX_CHANGES_VALUE", str(MAX_CHANGES))
)


def build_agent_source():
    return _AGENT_SOURCE


# Where arguments are passed on x86-64, by Process.platform; 32-bit code
# passes them on the stack.
_REGISTERS = {
    "windows": ("rcx", "rdx", "r8", "r9"),
    "linux": ("rdi", "rsi", "rdx", "rcx", "r8", "r9"),
}


def argument_name(index, platform, arch="x64"):
    """``rdi`` … for the register an argument is passed in, ``arg4`` on the stack."""
    registers = _REGISTERS.get(platform, ()) if arch == "x64" else ()
    return registers[index] if index < len(registers) else f"arg{index}"


_LOCATION = re.compile(r"^\s*([^\s+]+)\s*\+\s*(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+|[0-9]+)\s*$")


def parse_location(text):
    """The agent's spec of where a function is: an address, module+offset, or a name.

    ``0x55aa…`` is an address, ``BaldursGate+0x606e50`` a module and offset,
    anything else a symbol or export name. Raises ValueError for empty text.
    """
    text = text.strip()
    if not text:
        raise ValueError("no function given")
    if re.fullmatch(r"0x[0-9a-fA-F]+", text):
        return {"address": text.lower()}
    match = _LOCATION.match(text)
    if match:
        return {"module": match.group(1), "offset": int(match.group(2), 0)}
    return {"name": text}


def signed(value_text, bits=64):
    """The register value ``0x…`` as a signed number."""
    value = int(value_text, 16)
    return value - (1 << bits) if value >= 1 << (bits - 1) else value


def change_numbers(before, after):
    """(before, after) of a changed range as little-endian unsigned numbers, or None.

    Only for ranges of 1–8 bytes, the size of a number: longer ones are
    probably several fields.
    """
    size = len(before) // 2
    if not 1 <= size <= 8:
        return None
    return (int.from_bytes(bytes.fromhex(before), "little"),
            int.from_bytes(bytes.fromhex(after), "little"))


class NativeMonitorWorker(AgentWorker):
    """Keep a Frida session open for native function monitors; see the module documentation.

    The public methods are safe to call from the GUI thread; results come
    back through the signals.
    """

    # monitor id, {address, where, symbol, kind, function?, functionName?}
    added = Signal(int, object)
    removed = Signal(int)
    # calls, {monitor id: {calls, skipped}}
    calls = Signal(object, object)
    # monitor id, message: adding it failed
    add_failed = Signal(int, str)

    agent_name = "native monitor"
    agent_key = "native_monitor"

    def __init__(self, pid, parent=None):
        super().__init__(pid, parent)
        self.platform = None
        self.arch = None

    def agent_source(self):
        return build_agent_source()

    def add(self, monitor_id, location, arguments=DEFAULT_ARGUMENTS, dump=DEFAULT_DUMP,
            kind=AUTO):
        # pylint: disable=too-many-arguments,too-many-positional-arguments
        """Monitor the function or instruction at ``location`` (see parse_location).

        Expect added, with ``{address, where, symbol, kind}`` and for an
        instruction inside a known function ``function`` and ``functionName``.
        """
        spec = dict(location, id=monitor_id, kind=kind, args=arguments,
                    dump=min(dump, MAX_DUMP))
        self._commands.put(("add", spec))

    def remove(self, monitor_id):
        self._commands.put(("remove", monitor_id))

    @sessions.tracked(sessions.NATIVE_MONITOR)
    def run(self):
        self._run_agent()

    def _execute(self, api, action, argument):
        if action != "add":
            super()._execute(api, action, argument)
            return
        try:
            self.added.emit(argument["id"], api.add(argument))
        except frida.RPCException as error:
            # e.g. no such function: the other monitors go on
            self.add_failed.emit(argument["id"], messages.describe(error))

    def _run_command(self, api, action, argument):
        if action == "remove":
            api.remove(argument)
            self.removed.emit(argument)
        else:
            super()._run_command(api, action, argument)

    def _on_message(self, message, data):
        payload = message.get("payload") or {}
        if payload.get("kind") == "ready":
            self.platform = payload.get("platform")
            self.arch = payload.get("arch")
        super()._on_message(message, data)

    def _on_payload(self, kind, payload):
        if kind == "calls":
            self.calls.emit(payload.get("calls", []), {
                int(key): value for key, value in payload.get("counts", {}).items()})

```

`hermes/features/native_trace.js`:

```js
const FUNCTION_CAPACITY = FUNCTION_CAPACITY_VALUE;
const FIRST_CAPACITY = FIRST_CAPACITY_VALUE;
const EVENT_CAPACITY = EVENT_CAPACITY_VALUE;
const SYMBOL_BUDGET_MS = SYMBOL_BUDGET_VALUE;
const EVENT_SIZE = 32;
const THREAD_SIZE = 8;
const STOP_GC_TIMEOUT = 500;
// How long begin waits for callouts of the previous phase (ms).
const QUIESCE_TIMEOUT = 2000;
const DISPOSE_GC_TIMEOUT = 3000;
const PHASES = { baseline: 1, scenario: 2 };
const WINDOWS = Process.platform === 'windows';
const AGENT_THREAD = Process.getCurrentThreadId();
// Linux x86-64: free address space Stalker's thread contexts should land at
// the top of, see withRoomNearby.
const STEER_CONTEXTS = Process.platform === 'linux' && Process.arch === 'x64';
const LANDING_SIZE = 256n * 1024n * 1024n;
const STEER_PASSES = 8;

// The transform puts a callout before every call of the followed code; the
// callout runs in the game's thread, works out where the call goes and
// counts it. Functions sit in a hash table by address (slot = function to
// the C side), first calls per thread in another one.
const C_SOURCE = `
/* Frida 17.24's capstone.h stops TinyCC with a "#pragma message" for
   compilers it does not know; as __IBMC__ it takes the GCC attributes,
   which TinyCC understands. */
#define CAPSTONE_STATIC
#define __IBMC__ 1
#include <gum/gumstalker.h>
#undef __IBMC__

#define FUNCTIONS ${FUNCTION_CAPACITY}
#define FIRSTS ${FIRST_CAPACITY}
#define CAPACITY ${EVENT_CAPACITY}
#define PROBES 512

enum { TARGET_KNOWN, TARGET_REGISTER, TARGET_MEMORY };

typedef struct {
  guint32 seq;
  guint32 function;
  guint32 thread;
  guint32 reserved;
  guint64 caller;
  gint64 time;
} Event;

typedef struct {
  guint32 id;
  volatile gint left;  /* Windows: it called leave() */
} Thread;

typedef struct {
  gsize site;    /* the call instruction */
  gsize next;    /* the instruction after it: rip-relative operands */
  gsize target;  /* TARGET_KNOWN */
  guint32 thread;
  gint kind;
  gint base;     /* x86_reg */
  gint index;
  gint scale;
  gint64 disp;
  Thread * info;
} Site;

/* phase (0 off, 1 baseline, 2 scenario), events, lost calls, active
   callouts, threads to leave (Windows) */
extern volatile gint state[8];
/* Windows: Stalker.unfollow() of the calling thread */
extern void leave (void);
extern volatile gsize keys[];     /* function address per slot, 0: free */
extern volatile gint claims[];
extern volatile gint counts[];
extern volatile guint8 quiet[];   /* called in the baseline */
extern volatile gint first_claims[];
extern volatile gint first_functions[];  /* slot + 1 */
extern volatile gint first_threads[];
extern Event events[];

gint64 now (void) {
  return g_get_monotonic_time ();
}

/* Only the agent writes the phase. A locked add rather than a plain store:
   it is a full barrier, so the agent's following read of state[3] cannot
   pass it (the callouts' locked add on state[3] is the other half). */
void set_phase (gint phase) {
  g_atomic_int_add (&state[0], phase - state[0]);
}

static gsize read_register (GumCpuContext * c, gint reg, const Site * s) {
  switch (reg) {
#if defined (__x86_64__)
    case X86_REG_RAX: return c->rax;
    case X86_REG_RBX: return c->rbx;
    case X86_REG_RCX: return c->rcx;
    case X86_REG_RDX: return c->rdx;
    case X86_REG_RSI: return c->rsi;
    case X86_REG_RDI: return c->rdi;
    case X86_REG_RBP: return c->rbp;
    case X86_REG_RSP: return c->rsp;
    case X86_REG_R8: return c->r8;
    case X86_REG_R9: return c->r9;
    case X86_REG_R10: return c->r10;
    case X86_REG_R11: return c->r11;
    case X86_REG_R12: return c->r12;
    case X86_REG_R13: return c->r13;
    case X86_REG_R14: return c->r14;
    case X86_REG_R15: return c->r15;
    case X86_REG_RIP: return s->next;
#elif defined (__i386__)
    case X86_REG_EAX: return c->eax;
    case X86_REG_EBX: return c->ebx;
    case X86_REG_ECX: return c->ecx;
    case X86_REG_EDX: return c->edx;
    case X86_REG_ESI: return c->esi;
    case X86_REG_EDI: return c->edi;
    case X86_REG_EBP: return c->ebp;
    case X86_REG_ESP: return c->esp;
    case X86_REG_EIP: return s->next;
#else
# error "the native trace needs an x86 processor"
#endif
    default: return 0;  /* X86_REG_INVALID: no base or index */
  }
}

static gsize call_target (GumCpuContext * c, const Site * s) {
  gsize address;
  if (s->kind == TARGET_KNOWN)
    return s->target;
  if (s->kind == TARGET_REGISTER)
    return read_register (c, s->base, s);
  address = read_register (c, s->base, s) + read_register (c, s->index, s) * s->scale
      + (gsize) s->disp;
  return *(const gsize *) GSIZE_TO_POINTER (address);
}

/* No compare-and-swap in Frida's TinyCC: a thread takes a free entry by
   counting up its claims, the one that counted from 0 owns it and writes the
   key; the others wait for that. */

static gint function_slot (gsize target) {
  guint i = (guint) ((target >> 4) * 0x9E3779B1u) & (FUNCTIONS - 1);
  guint probe;
  for (probe = 0; probe < PROBES; probe++) {
    gsize key = keys[i];
    if (key == 0 && claims[i] == 0 && g_atomic_int_add (&claims[i], 1) == 0) {
      keys[i] = target;
      return i;
    }
    while (key == 0)  /* taken just now: the key is written next */
      key = keys[i];
    if (key == target)
      return i;
    i = (i + 1) & (FUNCTIONS - 1);
  }
  return -1;
}

static gboolean first_call (gint function, guint32 thread) {
  /* Whether this is the first call of function in thread: notes it if so. */
  guint i = ((guint) function * 0x9E3779B1u ^ thread * 0x85EBCA6Bu) & (FIRSTS - 1);
  guint probe;
  for (probe = 0; probe < PROBES; probe++) {
    gint t;
    if (first_claims[i] == 0 && g_atomic_int_add (&first_claims[i], 1) == 0) {
      first_functions[i] = function + 1;
      first_threads[i] = thread;  /* last: the entry is complete */
      return TRUE;
    }
    /* taken just now (begin may clear it meanwhile) */
    while ((t = first_threads[i]) == 0 && first_claims[i] != 0)
      ;
    if (t == (gint) thread && first_functions[i] == function + 1)
      return FALSE;
    i = (i + 1) & (FIRSTS - 1);
  }
  return FALSE;  /* full: the event capacity is long reached */
}

static void on_call (GumCpuContext * c, gpointer data) {
  const Site * s = data;
  gint phase;
  gsize target;
  gint slot, at;
  Event * event;
  g_atomic_int_add (&state[3], 1);
  /* Windows: the thread stops following itself, once. Stalker lets it go
     at the next block; taken over from outside, threads froze under Wine. */
  if (state[4] != 0 && s->info->left == 0 && g_atomic_int_add (&s->info->left, 1) == 0)
    leave ();
  phase = state[0];
  if (phase == 0)
    goto done;
  target = call_target (c, s);
  if (target == 0)
    goto done;
  slot = function_slot (target);
  if (slot < 0) {
    g_atomic_int_add (&state[2], 1);
    goto done;
  }
  g_atomic_int_add (&counts[slot], 1);
  if (phase != 2 || quiet[slot] || !first_call (slot, s->thread))
    goto done;
  at = g_atomic_int_add (&state[1], 1);
  if (at >= CAPACITY)
    goto done;
  event = &events[at];
  event->function = slot;
  event->thread = s->thread;
  event->caller = s->site;
  event->time = g_get_monotonic_time ();
  /* last: the reader skips events still being written */
  ((volatile Event *) event)->seq = at + 1;
done:
  g_atomic_int_add (&state[3], -1);
}

static Site * describe (const cs_insn * insn, Thread * thread) {
  const cs_x86_op * op = &insn->detail->x86.operands[0];
  Site * s;
  gsize next = insn->address + insn->size;
  if (op->type == X86_OP_IMM && (gsize) op->imm == next)
    return NULL;  /* call $+5: code reading its own address (32-bit PIC) */
  if (op->type == X86_OP_MEM && op->mem.segment != X86_REG_INVALID)
    return NULL;  /* fs:/gs: the segment's base is not in the context */
  if (op->type != X86_OP_IMM && op->type != X86_OP_REG && op->type != X86_OP_MEM)
    return NULL;
  s = g_malloc0 (sizeof (Site));
  s->site = insn->address;
  s->next = next;
  s->thread = thread->id;
  s->info = thread;
  if (op->type == X86_OP_IMM) {
    s->kind = TARGET_KNOWN;
    s->target = (gsize) op->imm;
  } else if (op->type == X86_OP_REG) {
    s->kind = TARGET_REGISTER;
    s->base = op->reg;
  } else {
    s->kind = TARGET_MEMORY;
    s->base = op->mem.base;
    s->index = op->mem.index;
    s->scale = op->mem.scale;
    s->disp = op->mem.disp;
  }
  return s;
}

void transform (GumStalkerIterator * iterator, GumStalkerOutput * output, gpointer user_data) {
  /* Runs in the followed thread whenever Stalker compiles a block of its code. */
  Thread * thread = user_data;
  const cs_insn * insn;
  while (gum_stalker_iterator_next (iterator, &insn)) {
    if (insn->id == X86_INS_CALL) {
      Site * site = describe (insn, thread);
      if (site != NULL)
        gum_stalker_iterator_put_callout (iterator, on_call, site, g_free);
    }
    gum_stalker_iterator_keep (iterator);
  }
}

void tally (guint64 * out) {
  /* calls and functions of the phase so far */
  guint64 calls = 0;
  guint64 functions = 0;
  guint i;
  for (i = 0; i < FUNCTIONS; i++) {
    guint count = counts[i];
    if (count != 0) {
      calls += count;
      functions++;
    }
  }
  out[0] = calls;
  out[1] = functions;
}
`;

let trace = null;
// Traces stopped: a thread blocked in a call since may come back into code
// with callouts into their CModule.
const retired = [];

function folder(path) {
  const cut = Math.max(path.lastIndexOf('/'), path.lastIndexOf('\\'));
  return (cut < 0 ? path : path.substring(0, cut + 1)).toLowerCase();
}

function isGameModule(module, gameFolder) {
  // The game's own code: the program and what lies in its folder tree.
  return module.path.toLowerCase().startsWith(gameFolder);
}

function programModule() {
  // The game's executable. Under Wine Frida's Process.mainModule is just the
  // first module it lists (e.g. netapi32.dll); Windows itself knows better.
  if (WINDOWS) {
    const getModuleHandle = new NativeFunction(
      Process.getModuleByName('kernel32.dll').getExportByName('GetModuleHandleW'),
      'pointer', ['pointer']);
    const module = Process.findModuleByAddress(getModuleHandle(NULL));
    if (module !== null)
      return module;
  }
  return Process.mainModule;
}

function threadLoads(ids, seconds) {
  // Windows: {id: share of a CPU} over ``seconds``, from GetThreadTimes (in
  // steps of the scheduler's tick, about 10 ms); null where unknown. Under
  // Wine the agent sees Windows thread ids, which /proc does not know.
  const kernel32 = Process.getModuleByName('kernel32.dll');
  const openThread = new NativeFunction(kernel32.getExportByName('OpenThread'),
                                        'pointer', ['uint32', 'int', 'uint32']);
  const closeHandle = new NativeFunction(kernel32.getExportByName('CloseHandle'),
                                         'int', ['pointer']);
  const getThreadTimes = new NativeFunction(kernel32.getExportByName('GetThreadTimes'), 'int',
                                            ['pointer', 'pointer', 'pointer', 'pointer', 'pointer']);
  const times = Memory.alloc(32);
  const THREAD_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION = 0x0800;

  function cpuTime(id) {
    // Kernel plus user time in 100 ns units, or null.
    const handle = openThread(THREAD_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, 0, id);
    if (handle.isNull())
      return null;
    try {
      if (!getThreadTimes(handle, times, times.add(8), times.add(16), times.add(24)))
        return null;
      return times.add(16).readU64().add(times.add(24).readU64());
    } finally {
      closeHandle(handle);
    }
  }

  const before = new Map(ids.map(id => [id, cpuTime(id)]));
  Thread.sleep(seconds);
  const loads = {};
  for (const id of ids) {
    const start = before.get(id);
    const end = cpuTime(id);
    loads[id] = start === null || end === null
      ? null : Number(end.sub(start)) / (seconds * 1e7);
  }
  return loads;
}

function inventory(measureSeconds = 0) {
  // ``measureSeconds``: measure the threads' load here (Windows only).
  const main = programModule();
  const gameFolder = folder(main.path);
  const modules = Process.enumerateModules();
  const threads = Process.enumerateThreads().filter(thread => thread.id !== AGENT_THREAD);
  const loads = WINDOWS && measureSeconds > 0
    ? threadLoads(threads.map(thread => thread.id), measureSeconds) : {};
  return {
    platform: Process.platform,
    threads: threads.map(thread => ({
      id: thread.id, name: thread.name || '', state: thread.state, load: loads[thread.id] ?? null
    })),
    modules: modules.map(module => ({
      name: module.name, path: module.path, base: module.base.toString(), size: module.size,
      game: module.name === main.name || isGameModule(module, gameFolder)
    }))
  };
}

function zero(pointer, length) {
  if (length > 0)
    pointer.writeByteArray(new ArrayBuffer(length));
}

// Windows: what the followed threads call to stop following themselves.
let leaveFunction = null;

function leaveCallback() {
  if (leaveFunction === null)
    leaveFunction = new NativeCallback(() => { Stalker.unfollow(); }, 'void', []);
  return leaveFunction;
}

// Windows: one Stalker serves every trace of this agent (two in one process
// froze a game on the second stop). What it excluded stays excluded, so a
// trace that follows such a module needs a fresh agent.
const FRESH_AGENT = 'needs a fresh agent';
const excludedModules = new Set();

function threadsLeft(t) {
  // Followed threads of trace ``t`` that left it, and the ids still in it.
  let left = 0;
  const staying = [];
  for (const [id, info] of t.threads) {
    if (info.add(4).readS32() !== 0)
      left++;
    else
      staying.push(id);
  }
  return { left, staying };
}

function stillFollowed() {
  // Windows: threads an earlier trace of this agent still follows.
  const ids = new Set();
  for (const t of retired) {
    if (t.leaving)
      threadsLeft(t).staying.forEach(id => ids.add(id));
  }
  return ids;
}

function compile(threadCount) {
  // The CModule and its memory, all of it zeroed.
  if (Process.arch !== 'x64' && Process.arch !== 'ia32')
    throw hermesError('error.native_trace.needs_x86', { arch: Process.arch });
  const memory = {
    state: Memory.alloc(32),
    keys: Memory.alloc(Process.pointerSize * FUNCTION_CAPACITY),
    claims: Memory.alloc(4 * FUNCTION_CAPACITY),
    counts: Memory.alloc(4 * FUNCTION_CAPACITY),
    quiet: Memory.alloc(FUNCTION_CAPACITY),
    first_claims: Memory.alloc(4 * FIRST_CAPACITY),
    first_functions: Memory.alloc(4 * FIRST_CAPACITY),
    first_threads: Memory.alloc(4 * FIRST_CAPACITY),
    events: Memory.alloc(EVENT_SIZE * EVENT_CAPACITY)
  };
  zero(memory.state, 32);
  zero(memory.keys, Process.pointerSize * FUNCTION_CAPACITY);
  zero(memory.claims, 4 * FUNCTION_CAPACITY);
  zero(memory.counts, 4 * FUNCTION_CAPACITY);
  zero(memory.quiet, FUNCTION_CAPACITY);
  const cm = new CModule(C_SOURCE, { ...memory, leave: leaveCallback() });
  const tallied = Memory.alloc(16);
  const tally = new NativeFunction(cm.tally, 'void', ['pointer']);
  return {
    ...memory, cm,
    now: new NativeFunction(cm.now, 'int64', []),
    setPhase: new NativeFunction(cm.set_phase, 'void', ['int']),
    tally() {
      tally(tallied);
      return [Number(tallied.readU64()), Number(tallied.add(8).readU64())];
    },
    threadInfo: Memory.alloc(THREAD_SIZE * Math.max(threadCount, 1))
  };
}

function start(spec) {
  // spec: { threads: [ids], modules: [names to follow], ranges: [[base, size]] to run natively }
  if (trace !== null)
    throw hermesError('error.native_trace.running');
  const followed = new Set(spec.modules);
  if (WINDOWS) {
    const excluded = spec.modules.filter(name => excludedModules.has(name));
    if (excluded.length > 0)
      throw new Error(`${FRESH_AGENT}: ${excluded.join(', ')} excluded by an earlier trace`);
  }
  // Threads an earlier trace still follows are left alone.
  const busy = WINDOWS ? stillFollowed() : new Set();
  const requested = spec.threads.filter(id => id !== AGENT_THREAD);
  const threadIds = requested.filter(id => !busy.has(id));
  const compiled = compile(threadIds.length);
  let included = 0;
  // The modules loaded now, also those loaded since the inventory. Only before
  // following: Stalker's exclusions must not change while threads compile
  // code (a module observer excluding modules loaded during the trace made
  // Baldur's Gate and Dark Souls III crash under Proton). Modules loaded
  // later are recompiled like the game's code.
  for (const module of Process.enumerateModules()) {
    if (followed.has(module.name)) {
      included++;
    } else {
      Stalker.exclude(module);  // runs natively: only calls into it are seen
      excludedModules.add(module.name);
    }
  }
  // Code Frida knows no module of (Wine's Unix side): runs natively as well.
  // A 32-bit game cannot reach the 64-bit libraries of the new WoW64.
  for (const [base, size] of spec.ranges || []) {
    if (Process.pointerSize === 4 && uint64(base).add(size).compare(uint64('0x100000000')) > 0)
      continue;
    Stalker.exclude({ base: ptr(base), size });
  }
  trace = {
    ...compiled,
    all: new ModuleMap(),
    slots: new Map(),       // slot of the C side -> function number
    index: new Map(),       // target address text -> function number
    functions: [],          // [address, module, offset]
    reported: 0,            // functions already sent to Python
    named: new Set(),       // functions whose name was looked up
    exports: new Map(),     // module name -> Map(address text -> export name)
    baseline: null,         // Uint8Array: slots called in the baseline
    phase: null,
    began: 0,
    beganMono: 0n,
    threads: [],            // [id, Thread of the C side]: followed
    entries: [],            // Windows: hooks threads enter Stalker through
    waiting: new Map()      // Windows: id -> Thread of the C side, not entered yet
  };
  const ids = threadIds;
  const infos = new Map(ids.map((id, i) => {
    const info = trace.threadInfo.add(THREAD_SIZE * i);
    info.writeU32(id);
    info.add(4).writeU32(0);
    return [id, info];
  }));
  let steered = null;
  const failed = WINDOWS
    ? enterOnReturn(trace, infos, new ModuleMap(module => followed.has(module.name)))
    : withRoomNearby(() => followAll(trace, infos), placed => { steered = placed; });
  return { threads: ids.length - failed.length,
           failed: failed.length + requested.length - ids.length, modules: included,
           waiting: trace.waiting.size, steered };
}

// --- Room for Stalker's code ---------------------------------------------------
// On x86-64 Stalker's code reaches its thread's context with 32-bit offsets,
// so every slab of code (4 MB) must lie within ±2 GB of the context. Gum
// asks the kernel for the context without a hint; the kernel puts it into
// the highest gap below mmap_base. A game that mapped many GB (EVERSPACE:
// 9.9 GB in 5700 regions, gaps of a few MB) leaves no 4 MB within ±2 GB of
// there: gum_memory_allocate_near fails, and Stalker writes to the NULL it
// got (SIGSEGV at 0x18 a moment after following). So while Stalker creates
// the contexts, every gap above the highest large free area is filled with
// placeholders: the contexts land at the top of that area, with room below.

let libcMmap = null;

function mmapFunctions() {
  if (libcMmap === null) {
    libcMmap = {
      mmap: new NativeFunction(Module.getGlobalExportByName('mmap'), 'pointer',
                               ['pointer', 'size_t', 'int', 'int', 'int', 'long']),
      munmap: new NativeFunction(Module.getGlobalExportByName('munmap'), 'int',
                                 ['pointer', 'size_t'])
    };
  }
  return libcMmap;
}

function mappedRanges() {
  // [[start, end]] (BigInt) of the mappings, without the stack and the
  // kernel's pages: hintless mappings never go above them.
  const ranges = [];
  for (const line of File.readAllText('/proc/self/maps').split('\n')) {
    if (line === '')
      continue;
    if (/\[(stack|vvar|vvar_vclock|vdso|vsyscall)\]$/.test(line))
      break;
    const [start, end] = line.split(' ', 1)[0].split('-');
    ranges.push([BigInt('0x' + start), BigInt('0x' + end)]);
  }
  return ranges;
}

function fillGapsAboveLanding(placed) {
  // Fill every gap above the highest gap of LANDING_SIZE; how many were filled.
  const { mmap } = mmapFunctions();
  const PROT_NONE = 0;
  const MAP_PRIVATE = 0x02, MAP_ANONYMOUS = 0x20, MAP_NORESERVE = 0x4000;
  const MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE = 0x100000;  // never over a mapping the game made meanwhile
  const ranges = mappedRanges();
  let landing = -1;
  for (let i = ranges.length - 1; i > 0 && landing < 0; i--) {
    if (ranges[i][0] - ranges[i - 1][1] >= LANDING_SIZE)
      landing = i;
  }
  if (landing < 0)
    return 0;
  let filled = 0;
  for (let i = landing + 1; i < ranges.length; i++) {
    const start = ranges[i - 1][1];
    const size = ranges[i][0] - start;
    if (size <= 0n)
      continue;
    const address = ptr(start.toString());
    const result = mmap(address, Number(size), PROT_NONE,
                        MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS | MAP_NORESERVE | MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE, -1, 0);
    if (result.equals(address)) {
      placed.push([address, Number(size)]);
      filled++;
    }
  }
  return filled;
}

function withRoomNearby(follow, report) {
  // Run ``follow`` (which creates Stalker's thread contexts) with the gaps
  // filled; ``report`` gets how many placeholders there were.
  if (!STEER_CONTEXTS)
    return follow();
  const placed = [];
  try {
    // Reading the map grows the agent's heap into the highest gaps: again
    // until no gap is left.
    for (let pass = 0; pass < STEER_PASSES; pass++) {
      if (fillGapsAboveLanding(placed) === 0)
        break;
    }
  } catch (_error) {
    // Without placeholders the contexts land where the kernel puts them.
  }
  try {
    return follow();
  } finally {
    const { munmap } = mmapFunctions();
    for (const [address, size] of placed)
      munmap(address, size);
    report(placed.length);
  }
}

function followAll(t, infos) {
  // Stalker takes each thread over where it stands; returns the ids it could not.
  const failed = [];
  for (const [id, info] of infos) {
    try {
      Stalker.follow(id, { transform: t.cm.transform, data: info });
      t.threads.push([id, info]);
    } catch (_error) {
      failed.push(id);  // e.g. ended meanwhile
    }
  }
  return failed;
}

function enterOnReturn(t, infos, followed) {
  // Windows: Stalker takes another thread over through a hardware breakpoint
  // at the instruction it stands at, mostly the return of a system call in
  // ntdll that Stalker's handler passes itself (it calls Sleep). Wine keeps
  // the breakpoint after the handler cleared it, so it hit again within the
  // handler, which then waited for a lock it held: the game froze, or (hit
  // later) crashed with EXCEPTION_SINGLE_STEP. Instead each thread follows
  // itself, which needs no breakpoint: a hook where it returns into the
  // followed code next (its stack's first return address there) starts
  // Stalker in the thread. Returns the ids of threads with no such address.
  const failed = [];
  const groups = new Map();  // address text -> {address, threads: Set of ids}
  const found = new Set();
  for (const thread of Process.enumerateThreads()) {
    if (!infos.has(thread.id))
      continue;
    found.add(thread.id);
    let target = null;
    try {
      target = Thread.backtrace(thread.context, Backtracer.FUZZY)
        .find(address => followed.find(address) !== null) || null;
    } catch (_error) {
      // no stack to read
    }
    if (target === null) {
      failed.push(thread.id);  // runs no followed code now: nothing to see
      continue;
    }
    const key = target.toString();
    if (!groups.has(key))
      groups.set(key, { address: target, threads: new Set() });
    groups.get(key).threads.add(thread.id);
    t.waiting.set(thread.id, infos.get(thread.id));
  }
  for (const id of infos.keys()) {
    if (!found.has(id))
      failed.push(id);  // ended meanwhile
  }
  for (const group of groups.values()) {
    try {
      group.listener = Interceptor.attach(group.address, function () {
        enter(t, group, this.threadId);
      });
      t.entries.push(group);
    } catch (_error) {
      for (const id of group.threads) {
        t.waiting.delete(id);
        failed.push(id);  // e.g. too short to hook
      }
    }
  }
  Interceptor.flush();
  return failed;
}

function enter(t, group, id) {
  // In the game's thread, at a hook of enterOnReturn: follow this thread.
  if (trace !== t || !group.threads.has(id))
    return;
  group.threads.delete(id);
  const info = t.waiting.get(id);
  t.waiting.delete(id);
  Stalker.follow(id, { transform: t.cm.transform, data: info });  // itself: no breakpoint
  t.threads.push([id, info]);
  if (group.threads.size === 0)
    setTimeout(() => detachEntry(t, group), 0);  // not from within its own callback
}

function detachEntry(t, group) {
  const index = t.entries.indexOf(group);
  if (index < 0)
    return;
  t.entries.splice(index, 1);
  group.listener.detach();
}

function functionNumber(target) {
  let number = trace.index.get(target);
  if (number === undefined) {
    number = trace.functions.length;
    trace.index.set(target, number);
    const address = ptr(target);
    const module = trace.all.find(address);
    trace.functions.push(module === null
      ? [target, '', null]
      : [target, module.name, address.sub(module.base).toInt32()]);
  }
  return number;
}

function readKeys(t) {
  const bytes = t.keys.readByteArray(Process.pointerSize * FUNCTION_CAPACITY);
  return Process.pointerSize === 8 ? new BigUint64Array(bytes) : new Uint32Array(bytes);
}

function slotNumbers(t, slots) {
  // Function numbers of C slots, numbering the ones not seen before.
  let keys = null;
  return slots.map(slot => {
    let number = t.slots.get(slot);
    if (number === undefined) {
      keys = keys || readKeys(t);
      number = functionNumber('0x' + keys[slot].toString(16));
      t.slots.set(slot, number);
    }
    return number;
  });
}

function requireTrace() {
  if (trace === null)
    throw hermesError('error.native_trace.not_running');
  return trace;
}

async function begin(phase) {
  const t = requireTrace();
  if (PHASES[phase] === undefined)
    throw hermesError('error.native_trace.unknown_phase', { phase });
  t.setPhase(0);  // calls from before belong to no phase
  t.phase = null;
  // Let callouts that observed the previous phase finish before clearing tables.
  const deadline = Date.now() + QUIESCE_TIMEOUT;
  while (t.state.add(12).readS32() !== 0) {
    if (Date.now() > deadline)
      throw hermesError('error.native_trace.thread_busy');
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1));
  }
  zero(t.counts, 4 * FUNCTION_CAPACITY);
  zero(t.first_claims, 4 * FIRST_CAPACITY);
  zero(t.first_functions, 4 * FIRST_CAPACITY);
  zero(t.first_threads, 4 * FIRST_CAPACITY);
  t.state.add(4).writeS32(0);
  t.state.add(8).writeS32(0);
  if (phase === 'scenario')
    zero(t.events, EVENT_SIZE * EVENT_CAPACITY);  // no seq of an earlier scenario
  if (phase === 'scenario' && t.baseline !== null)
    t.quiet.writeByteArray(t.baseline.buffer);
  else
    zero(t.quiet, FUNCTION_CAPACITY);
  t.phase = phase;
  t.began = Date.now();
  t.beganMono = BigInt(t.now().toString());
  t.setPhase(PHASES[phase]);
  return true;
}

function exportName(t, moduleName, target) {
  let names = t.exports.get(moduleName);
  if (names === undefined) {
    names = new Map();
    try {
      for (const found of Process.getModuleByName(moduleName).enumerateExports())
        names.set(found.address.toString(), found.name);
    } catch (_error) {
      // no exports to name it by
    }
    t.exports.set(moduleName, names);
  }
  return names.get(target) || null;
}

function symbolName(t, number) {
  // An export of that address, or (not under Windows: dbghelp under Wine)
  // a symbol of the module's symbol table or debug info.
  const [target, moduleName] = t.functions[number];
  if (moduleName === '')
    return null;
  const exported = exportName(t, moduleName, target);
  if (exported !== null || WINDOWS)
    return exported;
  try {
    const symbol = DebugSymbol.fromAddress(ptr(target));
    // Frida names an address without a symbol by its offset: "0x390"
    if (symbol.name !== null && !symbol.name.startsWith('0x') && symbol.address.equals(ptr(target)))
      return symbol.name;
  } catch (_error) {
    // unnamed
  }
  return null;
}

function callerText(t, address) {
  // ``module+0x…``, or the bare address for code outside modules.
  const module = t.all.find(address);
  return module === null ? address.toString() : `${module.name}+${address.sub(module.base)}`;
}

function readEvents(t) {
  // [[function number, thread, µs since the phase began, caller]] in call order.
  const written = t.state.add(4).readS32();
  const total = Math.min(written, EVENT_CAPACITY);
  const raw = [];
  if (total > 0) {
    const view = new DataView(t.events.readByteArray(total * EVENT_SIZE));
    for (let i = 0; i < total; i++) {
      const base = i * EVENT_SIZE;
      if (view.getUint32(base, true) !== i + 1)
        continue;
      raw.push([view.getUint32(base + 4, true), view.getUint32(base + 8, true),
                Number(view.getBigInt64(base + 24, true) - t.beganMono),
                view.getBigUint64(base + 16, true)]);
    }
  }
  const numbers = slotNumbers(t, raw.map(event => event[0]));
  const callers = new Map();
  return {
    events: raw.map(([_slot, thread, time, caller], i) => {
      let text = callers.get(caller);
      if (text === undefined) {
        text = callerText(t, ptr('0x' + caller.toString(16)));
        callers.set(caller, text);
      }
      return [numbers[i], thread, time, text];
    }),
    dropped: Math.max(0, written - EVENT_CAPACITY)
  };
}

function finish() {
  const t = requireTrace();
  const phase = t.phase;
  if (phase === null)
    throw hermesError('error.native_trace.not_recording');
  t.setPhase(0);
  t.phase = null;
  const duration = Date.now() - t.began;
  const slotCounts = new Uint32Array(t.counts.readByteArray(4 * FUNCTION_CAPACITY));
  const called = [];
  slotCounts.forEach((count, slot) => {
    if (count > 0)
      called.push(slot);
  });
  const counts = {};
  slotNumbers(t, called).forEach((number, i) => {
    counts[number] = slotCounts[called[i]];
  });
  const result = { phase, duration, counts, events: [], dropped: 0,
                   lost: t.state.add(8).readS32(), waiting: t.waiting.size };
  if (phase === 'scenario') {
    Object.assign(result, readEvents(t));
  } else {
    t.baseline = new Uint8Array(FUNCTION_CAPACITY);
    for (const slot of called)
      t.baseline[slot] = 1;
  }
  result.functions = t.functions.slice(t.reported);
  result.firstFunction = t.reported;
  t.reported = t.functions.length;
  // Names only for what the scenario called: the rows show nothing else.
  const names = {};
  const deadline = Date.now() + SYMBOL_BUDGET_MS;
  for (const key of phase === 'scenario' ? Object.keys(counts) : []) {
    const number = Number(key);
    if (t.named.has(number))
      continue;
    if (Date.now() > deadline)
      break;
    t.named.add(number);
    const name = symbolName(t, number);
    if (name !== null)
      names[number] = name;
  }
  result.names = names;
  return result;
}

function live() {
  const t = trace;
  if (t === null || t.phase === null)
    return;
  const [calls, methods] = t.tally();
  send({ kind: 'live', phase: t.phase, calls, methods,
         events: Math.min(t.state.add(4).readS32(), EVENT_CAPACITY) });
}

function stop() {
  // Exclusions stay with the Stalker (see FRESH_AGENT).
  if (trace === null)
    return null;
  const t = trace;
  trace = null;
  t.setPhase(0);
  for (const group of t.entries.slice())
    detachEntry(t, group);  // threads not entered yet stay as they are
  t.waiting.clear();
  if (WINDOWS) {
    // Each thread leaves at its next call (on_call): taking a thread over
    // from outside froze Baldur's Gate under Proton, looping in
    // NtSetContextThread.
    t.leaving = true;
    t.state.add(16).writeS32(1);
  } else {
    for (const [id] of t.threads) {
      try {
        Stalker.unfollow(id);
      } catch (_error) {
        // ended meanwhile
      }
    }
  }
  retired.push(t);
  return t;
}

async function waitForLeaving(t, timeout) {
  // Windows: until the threads of ``t`` left, or ``timeout`` ms; returns the
  // number still followed. A thread blocked in a call leaves once it returns.
  if (t === null || !t.leaving)
    return 0;
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeout;
  let staying = threadsLeft(t).staying;
  while (staying.length > 0 && Date.now() < deadline) {
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 20));
    staying = threadsLeft(t).staying;
  }
  return staying.length;
}

async function collect(timeout) {
  // Free the recompiled code once the threads have left it (garbageCollect:
  // whether some is still in use). A thread blocked in a call since it was
  // followed holds it until the call returns; Frida then frees it on unload.
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeout;
  while (Stalker.garbageCollect() && Date.now() < deadline)
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 20));
}

const liveTimer = setInterval(live, 500);
send({ kind: 'ready' });

rpc.exports = {
  inventory,
  start,
  begin,
  finish,
  async stop() {
    const stopped = stop();
    const staying = await waitForLeaving(stopped, STOP_GC_TIMEOUT);
    await collect(STOP_GC_TIMEOUT);
    return { stopped: stopped !== null, staying };
  },
  async dispose() {
    clearInterval(liveTimer);
    await waitForLeaving(stop(), DISPOSE_GC_TIMEOUT);
    await collect(DISPOSE_GC_TIMEOUT);
    return { staying: stillFollowed().size };
  }
};

```

`hermes/features/native_trace.py`:

```py
"""Native trace: which functions of a game's machine code a scenario runs.

The native counterpart of the Mono trace (trace.py), for games without
metadata: C++, own engines, Unreal, Godot, Source. Instead of hooking
methods it follows the game's threads with Frida's Stalker, which recompiles
the code they run and so sees every call, wherever it goes. It works like
Cheat Engine's "code filter":

1. ``inventory`` lists the threads and modules. ``start`` follows the chosen
   threads; the modules not chosen (system libraries, drivers) run natively,
   only the calls into them are seen. That keeps the game playable.
2. ``begin("baseline")`` … ``finish()`` counts the calls of every function
   while nothing happens in the game, ``begin("scenario")`` … ``finish()``
   while one does the thing of interest.

The answers have the shape of the Mono trace's, so ``analyze`` compares them
the same way: functions are numbered as the agent first sees them, the
numbers stay the same for the whole trace. A CModule counts the calls: its
Stalker ``transform`` puts a callout before every call instruction of the
followed code, which works out the target from the registers and counts it
in the game's thread. The sequence therefore holds the first call of every
function (not seen in the baseline) per thread in the exact order, with the
call instruction as the caller.

The table of functions holds ``FUNCTION_CAPACITY`` of them; calls of
functions beyond it are lost, the answers count them in ``lost``.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass

from PySide6.QtCore import Signal  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

import sys
import threading

import frida

from hermes.core import activity, messages, sessions, settings
from hermes.platform import is_wine_process, read_mappings
from hermes.features.trace import AgentWorker
from hermes.agent.source import MESSAGES_SOURCE, load_agent_source


# Functions the CModule's table can hold (a power of two; 17 bytes each).
FUNCTION_CAPACITY = 1 << 19
# (function, thread) pairs it notes first calls of at least (a power of two;
# 12 bytes each); twice the sequence's capacity when that is larger
FIRST_CAPACITY = 1 << 19
# First calls written into the sequence by default (setting trace_sequence);
# later ones are only counted.
EVENT_CAPACITY = 100_000
# The agent's answer when a trace needs a fresh agent (FRESH_AGENT in the agent).
FRESH_AGENT = "needs a fresh agent"
# How long ``finish`` may look up function names.
SYMBOL_BUDGET_MS = 3000
# How long the agent measures the threads' load under Wine (seconds), as
# thread_activity does on Linux.
WINE_LOAD_SECONDS = 0.5

_AGENT_TEMPLATE = MESSAGES_SOURCE + (
    load_agent_source(__file__)
    .replace("FUNCTION_CAPACITY_VALUE", str(FUNCTION_CAPACITY))
    .replace("SYMBOL_BUDGET_VALUE", str(SYMBOL_BUDGET_MS))
)


def first_capacity(event_capacity):
    """Entries of the table of first calls for a sequence of ``event_capacity``."""
    capacity = FIRST_CAPACITY
    while capacity < 2 * event_capacity:
        capacity *= 2
    return capacity


def build_agent_source(event_capacity=EVENT_CAPACITY):
    return (_AGENT_TEMPLATE
            .replace("FIRST_CAPACITY_VALUE", str(first_capacity(event_capacity)))
            .replace("EVENT_CAPACITY_VALUE", str(event_capacity)))


@dataclass
class NativeFunction:
    """A function the trace saw called: an address, by module where it has one."""

    address: int
    # "" for code outside any module (e.g. generated at run time)
    module: str
    offset: int | None
    # an export or symbol of exactly that address, or None
    symbol: str | None = None

    @property
    def location(self):
        """``module+0x…``, or the bare address."""
        if not self.module:
            return f"0x{self.address:x}"
        return f"{self.module}+0x{self.offset:x}"

    @property
    def label(self):
        """The symbol, or where it is."""
        return self.symbol or self.location

    @property
    def signature(self):
        """Everything known, for tooltips and the selection."""
        if self.symbol:
            return f"{self.symbol}  ({self.location}, 0x{self.address:x})"
        return f"{self.location}  (0x{self.address:x})"


def native_functions(rows):
    """NativeFunctions of the ``functions`` of a ``finish`` answer."""
    return [NativeFunction(int(address, 16), module, offset)
            for address, module, offset in rows]


def apply_names(functions, result):
    """Add the functions and names of a ``finish`` answer to ``functions``."""
    first = result.get("firstFunction", len(functions))
    if first != len(functions):
        raise ValueError(f"functions out of step: {first} instead of {len(functions)}")
    functions.extend(native_functions(result.get("functions", [])))
    for number, name in result.get("names", {}).items():
        functions[int(number)].symbol = name


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TraceThread:
    """A thread of the game, to follow or not."""

    id: int
    name: str
    # share of a CPU it used just now (0–1), None if unknown
    load: float | None = None
    # whether it ran just now at all, None if unknown
    active: bool | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TraceModule:
    """A module of the game; the game's own ones are followed by default."""

    name: str
    path: str
    base: int
    size: int
    game: bool


def foreign_code(mappings, followed):
    """[base, size] of the executable files mapped outside the ``followed`` TraceModules.

    Under Wine Frida knows only the PE modules: Wine's Unix side (ntdll.so,
    win32u.so, winex11.so, libc, the GL driver) is no module to exclude, so
    Stalker would recompile every system call down into the driver, Wine's
    syscall dispatcher included. Even one followed thread froze Baldur's Gate
    under Proton. Anonymous code stays followed: Stalker's own lies there.
    """
    spans = [(module.base, module.base + module.size) for module in followed]
    return [[hex(mapping.start), mapping.end - mapping.start] for mapping in mappings
            if "x" in mapping.permissions and mapping.path.startswith("/")
            and not any(mapping.start < end and start < mapping.end for start, end in spans)]


def _thread_times(pid, tid, proc_root="/proc"):
    """(CPU time in clock ticks, context switches) of a thread, or None."""
    task = f"{proc_root}/{pid}/task/{tid}"
    try:
        with open(f"{task}/stat", encoding="utf-8") as stat:
            fields = stat.read().rsplit(")", 1)[1].split()
        with open(f"{task}/status", encoding="utf-8") as status:
            # voluntary_ctxt_switches and nonvoluntary_ctxt_switches
            switches = sum(int(line.split(":", 1)[1]) for line in status
                           if "ctxt_switches:" in line)
    except (OSError, IndexError, ValueError):
        return None
    # fields[0] is the state (field 3): utime and stime are fields 14 and 15
    return int(fields[11]) + int(fields[12]), switches


def thread_activity(pid, tids, seconds=0.5, proc_root="/proc", sleep=None):
    """{tid: (share of a CPU, whether it ran)} over ``seconds``, for the tids /proc knows.

    A thread that only wakes up briefly uses less than a clock tick: whether
    it ran shows in its context switches (on Windows in its CPU cycles).
    """
    # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel
    import os
    import time

    sleep = sleep or time.sleep
    if sys.platform == "win32":
        from hermes.platform.windows import thread_times
        # (CPU seconds, CPU cycles)
        sample = thread_times
    else:
        ticks_per_second = os.sysconf("SC_CLK_TCK")  # pylint: disable=no-member

        def sample(tid):
            # (CPU seconds, context switches)
            times = _thread_times(pid, tid, proc_root)
            return None if times is None else (times[0] / ticks_per_second, times[1])

    before = {tid: sample(tid) for tid in tids}
    sleep(seconds)
    activity = {}
    for tid, start in before.items():
        end = sample(tid)
        if start is not None and end is not None:
            busy, woke = end[0] - start[0], end[1] - start[1]
            activity[tid] = (busy / seconds, busy > 0 or woke > 0)
    return activity


class NativeTraceWorker(AgentWorker):
    """Keep a Frida session open for a native trace; see the module documentation.

    The public methods are safe to call from the GUI thread; results come
    back through the signals.
    """

    # TraceThreads (the busiest first), TraceModules, platform
    inventory_found = Signal(object, object, str)
    # {threads, failed, modules}
    started = Signal(object)

    agent_name = "native trace"
    agent_key = "native_trace"

    def __init__(self, pid, parent=None):
        super().__init__(pid, parent)
        # Under Wine the agent sees Windows thread ids, which /proc does not
        # know: it measures their load itself.
        self._wine = is_wine_process(pid)
        # TraceModules of the last inventory
        self._modules = []
        # Agents of earlier traces: their Stalker keeps its exclusions, and
        # unloading one waits for threads still blocked in its code.
        self._retired = []
        self._traced = False
        # The agent runs on Windows (natively or under Wine), from the inventory.
        self._windows = False

    def agent_source(self):
        return build_agent_source(settings.get("trace_sequence"))

    def inventory(self):
        """List the threads and modules; expect inventory_found."""
        self._commands.put(("inventory", None))

    def trace(self, threads, modules):
        """Follow the thread ids ``threads`` in the modules named ``modules``."""
        self._commands.put(("start", {"threads": list(threads), "modules": list(modules)}))

    @sessions.tracked(sessions.NATIVE_TRACE)
    def run(self):
        self._run_agent()

    def _run_command(self, api, action, argument):
        if action == "inventory":
            if self._wine:
                # The agent measures with GetThreadTimes; whether a thread only
                # woke up briefly (less than a tick) cannot be told there.
                answer = api.inventory(WINE_LOAD_SECONDS)
                loads = {thread["id"]: (thread["load"], thread["load"] > 0)
                         for thread in answer["threads"] if thread.get("load") is not None}
            else:
                answer = api.inventory()
                ids = [thread["id"] for thread in answer["threads"]]
                loads = thread_activity(self.pid, ids)
            threads = [TraceThread(thread["id"], thread["name"],
                                   *loads.get(thread["id"], (None, None)))
                       for thread in answer["threads"]]
            threads.sort(key=lambda thread: -(thread.load or 0))
            modules = [TraceModule(module["name"], module["path"], int(module["base"], 16),
                                   module["size"], module["game"])
                       for module in answer["modules"]]
            self._modules = modules
            self._windows = answer["platform"] == "windows"
            self.inventory_found.emit(threads, modules, answer["platform"])
        elif action == "start":
            # Stalker keeps what it excluded: on Linux a new trace gets a fresh
            # agent. Under Windows one agent, and so one Stalker, serves every
            # trace (two froze a game); it asks for a fresh one only when a
            # module to follow was excluded before.
            if self._traced and not self._windows:
```
