```py
                api = self._fresh_agent()
            self._traced = True
            if self._wine:
                followed = [module for module in self._modules
                            if module.name in argument["modules"]]
                argument = {**argument,
                            "ranges": foreign_code(read_mappings(self.pid), followed)}
            activity.record("native_trace_start", pid=self.pid, threads=argument["threads"],
                            modules=argument["modules"],
                            native_ranges=len(argument.get("ranges", [])))
            try:
                answer = api.start(argument)
            except frida.RPCException as error:
                if FRESH_AGENT not in str(error):
                    raise
                answer = self._fresh_agent().start(argument)
            activity.record("native_trace_started", pid=self.pid, **answer)
            # Where the threads are once Stalker has taken them over (or not)
            timer = threading.Timer(1.0, activity.record_threads, (self.pid, "1 s after start"))
            timer.daemon = True
            timer.start()
            self.started.emit(answer)
        elif action == "stop":
            answer = api.stop()
            staying = answer.get("staying", 0) if isinstance(answer, dict) else 0
            if staying:
                # Windows: blocked in a call since; they leave once it returns.
                activity.record("native_trace_staying", pid=self.pid, threads=staying)
            self.stopped.emit()
            activity.record_threads(self.pid, "trace stopped")
        else:
            super()._run_command(api, action, argument)

    def _fresh_agent(self):
        """Keep the agent loaded (its Stalker may still hold threads) and load another."""
        self._retired.append(self._script)
        self._script = None
        self._load_script(self._session)
        return self._script.exports_sync

    def _unload_script(self):
        super()._unload_script()
        while self._retired:
            self._script = self._retired.pop()
            super()._unload_script()

```

`hermes/features/ptrace_watch.py`:

```py
"""A ptrace-backed hardware watchpoint monitor for process memory.

This is an alternative to the Frida watch backend (see write_watch.py). Instead
of injecting an agent it drives the Linux ``ptrace`` API directly, so it works
on targets Frida cannot instrument, most notably Wine/Proton processes. The
low-level ptrace machinery lives in :mod:`hermes.attach.ptrace_engine`; this
module turns watchpoint traps into the hit records the UI shows.
"""

import errno
import time

from PySide6.QtCore import Signal  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

from hermes.core import messages, sessions
from hermes.core.memory import read_memory
from hermes.attach.ptrace_engine import (
    MAX_INSTRUCTION_SIZE,
    SYNC_WINDOW,
    PtraceWatchpointEngine,
    build_dr7,
    decode_access,
    watch_alignment_error,
)

__all__ = ["PtraceWriteWatchWorker", "build_dr7", "decode_access"]


class PtraceWriteWatchWorker(PtraceWatchpointEngine):
    """Report writes (and, with ``reads``, reads) via ptrace watchpoints.

    Matches :class:`hermes.features.write_watch.WriteWatchWorker`'s interface so
    the two backends are interchangeable. Each hit tells whether its
    instruction ``read`` and/or ``write``-s the target.
    """

    monitor_ready = Signal(int, str)
    hits_ready = Signal(object)
    monitor_warning = Signal(str)
    monitor_failed = Signal(str)
    monitor_stopped = Signal()

    FLUSH_INTERVAL = 0.1

    def __init__(self, pid, address, size, parent=None, reads=False):
        # pylint: disable=too-many-arguments
        super().__init__(pid, parent)
        self.address = address
        self.size = size
        self.reads = reads
        self._slots = {0: (address, size, reads)}
        self._pending = {}
        self._access_cache = {}

    @sessions.tracked(sessions.PTRACE_WATCH)
    def run(self):
        """Attach, report hits until stopped, then detach cleanly."""
        try:
            self._monitor()
        except OSError as error:
            if not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                self.monitor_failed.emit(self._explain(error))
        finally:
            self._detach_all()
            self.monitor_stopped.emit()

    def _monitor(self):
        unaligned = watch_alignment_error(self.address, self.size)
        if unaligned is not None:
            raise OSError(errno.EINVAL, unaligned)
        self._load_mappings()
        warnings = self._attach_all()
        if not self._armed:
            raise messages.LocalizedOSError("error.ptrace_watch.no_thread", 1)
        self.monitor_ready.emit(len(self._armed), "")
        for message in warnings:
            self.monitor_warning.emit(message)

        last_flush = time.monotonic()
        while not self.isInterruptionRequested():
            if not self._pump():
                if time.monotonic() - last_flush >= self.FLUSH_INTERVAL:
                    self._flush()
                    last_flush = time.monotonic()
                time.sleep(0.002)
        self._flush()
        if self._target_gone:
            self.monitor_failed.emit(messages.text("error.ptrace.exited"))

    def _handle_trap(self, tid, slot, pc, bits):
        read, write = self._access_of(pc, bits)
        key = hex(pc)
        hit = self._pending.get(key)
        now = int(time.time() * 1000)
        if hit is not None:
            hit["count"] += 1
            hit["read"] = hit["read"] or read
            hit["write"] = hit["write"] or write
            hit["threadId"] = tid
            hit["time"] = now
            return
        self._pending[key] = {
            "pc": key,
            "site": self._site(pc),
            "value": None,
            "read": read,
            "write": write,
            "threadId": tid,
            "count": 1,
            "time": now,
        }

    def _access_of(self, pc, bits):
        cached = self._access_cache.get(pc)
        if cached is not None:
            return cached
        start = max(0, pc - (SYNC_WINDOW + MAX_INSTRUCTION_SIZE))
        data, readable = read_memory(self.pid, start, pc - start)
        if not all(readable):
            access = (self.reads, True)
        else:
            access = decode_access(bytes(data), len(data), bits, self.reads)
        self._access_cache[pc] = access
        return access

    def _read_value(self):
        data, readable = read_memory(self.pid, self.address, self.size)
        if not all(readable):
            return "unreadable"
        return " ".join(f"{byte:02x}" for byte in data)

    def _flush(self):
        if not self._pending:
            return
        hits = list(self._pending.values())
        self._pending.clear()
        value = self._read_value()
        for hit in hits:
            hit["value"] = value
        self.hits_ready.emit(hits)

```

`hermes/features/scripts.py`:

```py
"""Scripts: JavaScript that calls game code by time, e.g. a cheat every minute.

A script is a function body (like the ``code`` of a method script, see
``hermes.hooks.transforms``) that runs on the game thread, where game code
may be called (``engine.onMainThread``; Unreal: the next time it enters
ProcessEvent, Mono: mono_runtime_invoke on Unity's main thread). When it
runs is its ``mode``:

``"once"``    some ``seconds`` after it is started (each time hermes attaches)
``"repeat"``  every ``seconds``; the next run is timed when one has ended
``"manual"``  only when asked (``run_now``)

The body gets one ``ctx`` object:

    ctx.find("ClassName")   a live object of that class or a subclass
                            (Unreal, Unity), e.g. ctx.find("AlabamaCheatManager");
                            Unreal: searched for once (tens of ms on the
                            game thread), then only checked while it lives
    ctx.find("ClassName", "ObjectName")   the one of that name, e.g.
                            ctx.find("UnityEngine.GameObject", "Player(Clone)")
                            or ctx.find("BP_Hero_C", "BP_Hero_C_1"); Unreal
                            also by the name in its outer (ctx.outerName),
                            e.g. "AttributeStatsWidget.PointsAvailableTracker".
                            Class default objects and templates (a widget of
                            a Widget Blueprint's tree) are never found.
    ctx.forEach("ClassName", obj => ...)   calls the function for every object
                            ctx.find could give (until it returns false) and
                            gives how many; Unreal: reads every object anew
    ctx.outerName(obj)      Unreal: the object's name after its outer's,
                            "AttributeStatsWidget.PointsAvailableTracker" (a
                            widget's outer is the widget showing it)
    ctx.call("Namespace.Class.Method", ...args)   call a static game method
                     (also "Namespace.Class:Method", as the catalog names it)
    ctx.gas          Unreal games with the Gameplay Ability System: the
                     player's attributes. ctx.gas.get("Might") or
                     ctx.gas.get("AttributeSetCore.Might"): {base, current}
                     (null without a player); ctx.gas.setBase(name, value)
                     sets the base value through the game's own code, which
                     applies the active effects to it; ctx.gas.attributes()
                     lists the sets (see ScriptWorker.gas_attributes)
    ctx.findClass("ClassName")   Unreal: the class itself, e.g. for a
                     TSubclassOf parameter: ctx.findClass("ItFo_Potion_Health_03")
    ctx.args         the values of the script's parameters by name (see below)
    ctx.lang         the app language ("de" or "en")
    ctx.log(...)     output shown in the script log
    ctx.state        per-script object that persists between runs
    ctx.runs         how often it ran before
    ctx.scriptId

Objects are the wrappers method hooks get (``.call(name, ...args)``,
``.field(name)``, fields and properties as properties, methods as functions,
e.g. ``player.GetComponentByName("CharacterStats")``, ``.name``,
``.className``); a value
the body returns is shown as its result, an object with a ``target`` the
object inspector opens (``inspect``, ``evaluate`` and ``full_text`` work as
the method monitor's). Example (Avowed)::

    const cheats = ctx.find("AlabamaCheatManager");
    cheats.call("GiveHealth", 50);

A script may have parameters (``ScriptParam``): typed in when it is run by
hand, their defaults when it runs by time. A parameter is text, a number, a
bool or a choice; a choice's ``options`` is a function body like the
script's that returns the choices (asked for when they are to be shown, on
the game thread): values or ``{label, value}``, values being strings,
numbers or bools. Example (Gothic 1 Remake)::

    return ctx.call("CheatModeHelper:GetAllItems", "").map(item => ({
        label: String(item.m_Name), value: item.className}));

and the script gives the chosen item (``ctx.findClass(ctx.args.item)``).

Scripts live in the method monitor's agent (``hermes.features.monitor``),
in a Frida session of their own.
"""

import itertools
import json
import queue
import re
import threading
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import frida
from PySide6.QtCore import QThread, Signal  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

from hermes.core import logs, messages
from hermes.core import sessions
from hermes.attach.frida_attach import CLEANUP_ERRORS, FRIDA_ERRORS, attach_session
from hermes.features.monitor import build_agent_source


MODES = ("once", "repeat", "manual")
# A repeating script runs at most this often
MIN_REPEAT_SECONDS = 0.1
# What a parameter's value is
PARAM_KINDS = ("text", "number", "bool", "choice")
_PARAM_NAME = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$")
_TRUE = {"true", "1", "ja", "yes", "wahr"}
_FALSE = {"false", "0", "nein", "no", "falsch", ""}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ScriptParam:
    """A parameter of a script: ``ctx.args.<name>``.

    ``default`` is the value as typed in (a choice's: its value as text, or
    empty for none); ``options`` the function body that gives a choice's
    choices (see the module's docstring).
    """

    name: str
    label: str = ""
    kind: str = "text"
    default: str = ""
    options: str = ""

    def __post_init__(self):
        if not _PARAM_NAME.match(self.name):
            raise messages.LocalizedValueError("error.scripts.param_name", name=self.name)
        if self.kind not in PARAM_KINDS:
            raise messages.LocalizedValueError("error.scripts.param_kind",
                                              kinds=", ".join(PARAM_KINDS))
        if self.kind == "choice" and not self.options.strip():
            raise messages.LocalizedValueError("error.scripts.param_options", name=self.name)
        self.value(self.default)  # a default that is no value of its kind

    def value(self, text):
        """The value of ``text`` typed in for this parameter (not a choice's:
        its value is the chosen option's); raises LocalizedValueError."""
        if self.kind == "number":
            cleaned = text.strip().replace(",", ".")
            if cleaned == "":
                return 0
            try:
                return int(cleaned)
            except ValueError:
                pass
            try:
                return float(cleaned)
            except ValueError:
                raise messages.LocalizedValueError("error.scripts.param_number",
                                                  name=self.name, text=text) from None
        if self.kind == "bool":
            word = text.strip().lower()
            if word in _TRUE:
                return True
            if word in _FALSE:
                return False
            raise messages.LocalizedValueError("error.scripts.param_bool",
                                              name=self.name, text=text)
        if self.kind == "choice":
            return text if text != "" else None
        return text

    def to_json(self):
        return {"name": self.name, "label": self.label, "kind": self.kind,
                "default": self.default, "options": self.options}

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, data):
        return cls(str(data["name"]), str(data.get("label", "")), str(data.get("kind", "text")),
                   str(data.get("default", "")), str(data.get("options", "")))


def params_to_json(params):
    """The parameters as the database keeps them: JSON text, or None without any."""
    return json.dumps([param.to_json() for param in params]) if params else None


def params_from_json(text):
    """The parameters of a saved script (see params_to_json)."""
    return tuple(ScriptParam.from_json(data) for data in json.loads(text)) if text else ()


def choice_matches(value, text):
    """Whether a choice's option ``value`` is the one saved as ``text``."""
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return str(value).lower() == text.lower()
    if isinstance(value, float) and value.is_integer():
        return str(int(value)) == text
    return str(value) == text


@dataclass
class ScriptSpec:
    """The code of a script and when it runs (see the module's docstring)."""

    source: str
    mode: str = "manual"
    seconds: float = 0.0
    enabled: bool = True
    label: str = ""
    params: tuple = field(default_factory=tuple)

    def __post_init__(self):
        if self.mode not in MODES:
            raise messages.LocalizedValueError("error.scripts.mode", modes=", ".join(MODES))
        if self.seconds < 0:
            raise messages.LocalizedValueError("error.scripts.negative_seconds")
        if self.mode == "repeat" and self.seconds < MIN_REPEAT_SECONDS:
            raise messages.LocalizedValueError("error.scripts.repeat_minimum",
                                              seconds=MIN_REPEAT_SECONDS)
        self.params = tuple(self.params)
        names = [param.name for param in self.params]
        for name in names:
            if names.count(name) > 1:
                raise messages.LocalizedValueError("error.scripts.param_twice", name=name)

    def default_args(self):
        """``ctx.args`` of a run without asking: each parameter's default."""
        return {param.name: param.value(param.default) for param in self.params}

    def to_agent(self, script_id):
        return {
            "id": script_id,
            "source": self.source,
            "mode": self.mode,
            "seconds": self.seconds,
            "enabled": self.enabled,
            "args": self.default_args(),
            "options": {param.name: param.options for param in self.params
                        if param.kind == "choice"},
        }


class ScriptWorker(QThread):
    """Keep a Frida session open and run the scripts of one process.

    The public methods are safe to call from the GUI thread; results come
    back through the signals.
    """

    script_added = Signal(int)
    script_updated = Signal(int)
    script_removed = Signal(int)
    # script id, error text (compiling it, or a command failed)
    script_failed = Signal(int, str)
    # script id, {time, runs, result, target?, logs, error}
    script_ran = Signal(int, object)
    # As MethodMonitorWorker's, for the object inspector (see hermes.ui.widgets.inspection)
    inspected = Signal(int, object)
    inspect_failed = Signal(int, str)
    evaluated = Signal(int, object)
    evaluate_failed = Signal(int, str)
    methods_listed = Signal(int, object)
    methods_failed = Signal(int, str)
    call_described = Signal(int, object)
    called = Signal(int, object)
    call_failed = Signal(int, str)
    text_fetched = Signal(int, object)
    text_failed = Signal(int, str)
    # request id, the player's GAS attributes (see gas_attributes) or None
    gas_listed = Signal(int, object)
    gas_failed = Signal(int, str)
    # request id, {base, current} after setting a base value
    gas_set = Signal(int, object)
    gas_set_failed = Signal(int, str)
    # request id, a choice parameter's options [{label, value}] (see script_options)
    options_listed = Signal(int, object)
    options_failed = Signal(int, str)
    agent_log = Signal(str, str)
    worker_failed = Signal(str)

    _ids = itertools.count(1)
    _requests = itertools.count(1)

    def __init__(self, pid, parent=None, language="en"):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.pid = pid
        self.language = language
        self._commands = queue.Queue()
        self._ready = threading.Event()
        self._agent_error = None
        self._detach_reason = None

    def add_script(self, spec):
        """Queue a ScriptSpec and return its script id."""
        script_id = next(self._ids)
        self._commands.put(("add", script_id, spec))
        return script_id

    def update_script(self, script_id, spec):
        self._commands.put(("update", script_id, spec))

    def remove_script(self, script_id):
        self._commands.put(("remove", script_id, None))

    def run_now(self, script_id, args=None):
        """Run a script now; ``args`` are its ``ctx.args`` (else the defaults)."""
        self._commands.put(("run", script_id, args))

    def script_options(self, script_id, name):
        """The options of the choice parameter ``name``, from its code on the
        game thread; expect options_listed or options_failed."""
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("options", request_id, (script_id, name)))
        return request_id

    def inspect(self, target):
        """Read an object (a result's ``target``); expect inspected or inspect_failed."""
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("inspect", request_id, target))
        return request_id

    def evaluate(self, target, names):
        """Call the named getters of an object on the game's main thread."""
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("evaluate", request_id, (target, list(names))))
        return request_id

    def list_methods(self, target):
        """List the instance methods of an object (see MethodMonitorWorker)."""
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("methods", request_id, target))
        return request_id

    def describe_method(self, method):
        """Read the parameters of an instance method (see MethodMonitorWorker)."""
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("describe_method", request_id, method))
        return request_id

    def call_on(self, target, method, arguments):
        """Call an instance method on an object (see MethodMonitorWorker)."""
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("call_on", request_id, (target, method, list(arguments))))
        return request_id

    def gas_attributes(self):
        """Read the player's GAS attribute sets (Unreal); expect gas_listed or gas_failed.

        The answer is ``{owner, setter, component, sets: [{name, className,
        attributes: [{name, base, current}]}]}``, or None without a player.
        """
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("gas_attributes", request_id, ()))
        return request_id

    def gas_set_base(self, name, value):
        """Set the base value of the player's attribute ``name`` ("Set.Attribute")
        through the game; expect gas_set or gas_set_failed."""
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("gas_set_base", request_id, (name, float(value))))
        return request_id

    def full_text(self, text_id):
        """Fetch the whole text of a long string value (its ``fullText``)."""
        request_id = next(self._requests)
        self._commands.put(("text", request_id, text_id))
        return request_id

    @sessions.tracked(sessions.SCRIPTS)
    def run(self):
        session = None
        script = None
        try:
            session = attach_session(self.pid)
            sessions.SESSIONS.set_frida_session(self, session)
            session.on("detached", self._on_detached)
            script = session.create_script(build_agent_source(self.language))
            script.on("message", self._on_message)
            script.set_log_handler(self._on_log)
            script.load()
            if not self._ready.wait(5):
                raise messages.LocalizedRuntimeError("error.scripts.load_timeout")
            while (not self.isInterruptionRequested() and self._detach_reason is None
                   and self._agent_error is None):
                try:
                    command = self._commands.get(timeout=0.05)
                except queue.Empty:
                    continue
                self._execute(script.exports_sync, *command)
            if self._agent_error and not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                raise RuntimeError(self._agent_error)
            if self._detach_reason and not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                raise messages.LocalizedRuntimeError("error.agent.detached",
                                                     reason=self._detach_reason)
        except FRIDA_ERRORS + (OSError, RuntimeError) as error:
            if not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                self.worker_failed.emit(messages.describe(error))
        finally:
            if script is not None:
                try:
                    script.exports_sync.dispose()
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)
                try:
                    script.unload()
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)
            if session is not None:
                try:
                    session.detach()
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)

    def _execute(self, api, action, script_id, argument):
        try:
            if action == "add":
                api.add_script(argument.to_agent(script_id))
                self.script_added.emit(script_id)
            elif action == "update":
                api.update_script(script_id, argument.to_agent(script_id))
                self.script_updated.emit(script_id)
            elif action == "remove":
                if api.remove_script(script_id):
                    self.script_removed.emit(script_id)
            elif action == "run":
                api.run_script_now(script_id, argument)
            elif action in self._REQUESTS:
                self._answer(api, action, script_id, argument)
                return
        except frida.RPCException as error:
            self.script_failed.emit(script_id, messages.describe(error))

    # request action -> (agent call, answer signal, failure signal)
    _REQUESTS = {
        "inspect": ("inspect", "inspected", "inspect_failed"),
        "evaluate": ("evaluate", "evaluated", "evaluate_failed"),
        "methods": ("list_methods", "methods_listed", "methods_failed"),
        "describe_method": ("describe_method", "call_described", "call_failed"),
        "call_on": ("call_on", "called", "call_failed"),
        "text": ("full_text", "text_fetched", "text_failed"),
        "gas_attributes": ("gas_attributes", "gas_listed", "gas_failed"),
        "gas_set_base": ("gas_set_base", "gas_set", "gas_set_failed"),
        "options": ("script_options", "options_listed", "options_failed"),
    }

    def _answer(self, api, action, request_id, argument):
        call, answered, failed = self._REQUESTS[action]
        # Requests with several arguments queue them as a tuple
        arguments = argument if isinstance(argument, tuple) else (argument,)
        try:
            getattr(self, answered).emit(request_id, getattr(api, call)(*arguments))
        except frida.RPCException as error:
            getattr(self, failed).emit(request_id, messages.describe(error))

    def _on_message(self, message, _data):
        if message.get("type") == "error":
            self._agent_error = messages.describe(
                message.get("stack", messages.text("error.scripts.agent_failed")))
            self._ready.set()
            return
        payload = message.get("payload", {})
        kind = payload.get("kind")
        if kind == "ready":
            self._ready.set()
        elif kind == "script-run":
            self.script_ran.emit(payload.get("scriptId", 0), payload)

    def _on_log(self, level, text):
        logs.agent_log("script agent", level, text)
        self.agent_log.emit(level, text)

    def _on_detached(self, reason, _crash):
        self._detach_reason = reason

```

`hermes/features/trace.js`:

```js
const EVENT_CAPACITY = EVENT_CAPACITY_VALUE;
const EVENT_SIZE = 32;
const PHASES = { baseline: 1, scenario: 2 };

// Runs in the game's threads on every call of a traced method.
const C_SOURCE = `
#include <gum/guminterceptor.h>

#define CAPACITY ${EVENT_CAPACITY}

typedef struct {
  guint32 seq;
  guint32 method;
  guint32 thread;
  guint32 reserved;
  guint64 caller;
  gint64 time;
} Event;

extern volatile gint state[2];  /* phase (0 off, 1 baseline, 2 scenario), events written */
extern volatile gint counts[];
extern volatile guint8 quiet[];
extern Event events[];

gint64 now (void) {
  return g_get_monotonic_time ();
}

void on_enter (GumInvocationContext * ic) {
  gint phase = state[0];
  if (phase == 0)
    return;
  guint index = GPOINTER_TO_UINT (gum_invocation_context_get_listener_function_data (ic));
  g_atomic_int_add (&counts[index], 1);
  if (phase != 2 || quiet[index])
    return;
  gint slot = g_atomic_int_add (&state[1], 1);
  if (slot >= CAPACITY)
    return;
  Event * event = &events[slot];
  event->method = index;
  event->thread = gum_invocation_context_get_thread_id (ic);
  event->caller = GPOINTER_TO_SIZE (gum_invocation_context_get_return_address (ic));
  event->time = g_get_monotonic_time ();
  /* last: the reader skips events still being written */
  ((volatile Event *) event)->seq = slot + 1;
}
`;

let trace = null;
// Stopped traces: a game thread may still be in their code, writing to their
// memory.
const retired = [];
// The agent's own thread (RPCs run there); hooks run on game threads.
const AGENT_THREAD = Process.getCurrentThreadId();

function pauseForHooking() {
  // Many hooks change at once: stop the game's threads meanwhile, so none
  // enters code Frida is still changing (see pauseThreads). Never from a game
  // thread: it may hold locks the others need.
  return Process.getCurrentThreadId() === AGENT_THREAD ? pauseThreads() : null;
}

function resumeAfterHooking(paused) {
  Interceptor.flush();  // write the pending changes before the game runs on
  resumeThreads(paused);
}

// assembly -> tokens of the methods to trace next, sent in parts (choose):
// one message to Frida's gadget under Wine must stay below 128 KiB.
let tokens = new Map();

function choose(part) {
  // Add [[assembly, [token, ...]], ...] to the methods start() traces.
  for (const [assembly, wanted] of part) {
    if (!tokens.has(assembly))
      tokens.set(assembly, []);
    tokens.get(assembly).push(...wanted);
  }
  return true;
}

async function select(spec) {
  // The chosen methods: Hermes chose them by the catalog (see trace.py),
  // counting in spec.skipped those that cannot be traced.
  const chosenTokens = tokens;
  tokens = new Map();
  const chosen = [];
  for (const [assembly, wanted] of chosenTokens) {
    for (const found of await engine.methodsByToken(assembly, wanted))
      chosen.push({ assembly, ...found });
  }
  return { chosen, skipped: { ...spec.skipped } };
}

// Interceptors set at a time before other scripts of the agent get a turn
const ATTACH_CHUNK = 500;
const DISPOSE_TIMEOUT = 5000;
let starting = false;
let cancelled = false;

function reporter(step, total, current = () => '') {
  // A progress callback for a batch that reports each state once.
  let reported = -1;
  return done => {
    if (done === reported)
      return;  // the same method still: name it, should Mono hang there
    reported = done;
    send({ kind: 'progress', step, done, total, current: done < total ? current(done) : '' });
  };
}

function nextTurn() {
  return new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 0));
}

async function start(spec) {
  if (trace !== null || starting)
    throw hermesError('error.trace.running');
  starting = true;
  cancelled = false;
  try {
    return await prepare(spec);
  } finally {
    starting = false;
  }
}

async function prepare(spec) {
  const selected = await select(spec);
  const skipped = { ...selected.skipped, com: 0 };
  // Compiling code that uses COM interop hangs Mono on Linux: leave it out.
  const usesCom = await engine.checkAll(selected.chosen.map(found => found.method),
    reporter('check', selected.chosen.length, done => selected.chosen[done].entry[5]));
  const chosen = selected.chosen.filter((_found, i) => !usesCom[i]);
  skipped.com = selected.chosen.length - chosen.length;
  const total = chosen.length;
  const codes = await engine.compileAll(chosen.map(found => found.method),
    reporter('compile', total, done => chosen[done].entry[5]));
  const size = Math.max(total, 1);
  const memory = {
    state: Memory.alloc(8),
    counts: Memory.alloc(4 * size),
    quiet: Memory.alloc(size),
    events: Memory.alloc(EVENT_SIZE * EVENT_CAPACITY)
  };
  const cm = new CModule(C_SOURCE, memory);
  trace = {
    ...memory, cm, now: new NativeFunction(cm.now, 'int64', []),
    methods: [], listeners: [], starts: [], phase: null, baseline: null
  };
  const paused = pauseForHooking();
  let counts;
  try {
    counts = await attachAll(codes, chosen, cm);
  } finally {
    resumeAfterHooking(paused);
  }
  trace.starts.sort((a, b) => a.compare(b));
  updateUnmapWatch();
  return { methods: trace.methods, skipped, ...counts };
}

async function attachAll(codes, chosen, cm) {
  // Hook the code of every method; returns { notCompiled, failed }.
  const total = codes.length;
  const seen = new Set();
  let notCompiled = 0;
  let failed = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < codes.length; i++) {
    if (i % ATTACH_CHUNK === 0) {
      send({ kind: 'progress', step: 'attach', done: i, total });
      await nextTurn();
      if (cancelled) {
        stop();
        throw new Error('cancelled');
      }
    }
    const code = codes[i];
    if (code === null) {
      notCompiled++;
      continue;
    }
    const key = code.start.toString();
    if (seen.has(key))
      continue;  // shared code: counted under the first method
    const index = trace.methods.length;
    try {
      trace.listeners.push(Interceptor.attach(code.start, { onEnter: cm.on_enter }, ptr(index)));
    } catch (_error) {
      failed++;  // e.g. too short to intercept
      continue;
    }
    seen.add(key);
    trace.starts.push(code.start);
    const found = chosen[i];
    trace.methods.push([found.assembly, found.className, ...found.entry]);
  }
  return { notCompiled, failed };
}

function requireTrace() {
  if (trace === null)
    throw hermesError('error.trace.not_running');
  return trace;
}

function zero(pointer, length) {
  if (length > 0)
    pointer.writeByteArray(new ArrayBuffer(length));
}

function begin(phase) {
  const t = requireTrace();
  if (PHASES[phase] === undefined)
    throw hermesError('error.trace.unknown_phase', { phase });
  t.state.writeS32(0);
  const n = t.methods.length;
  zero(t.counts, 4 * n);
  t.state.add(4).writeS32(0);
  if (phase === 'scenario')
    zero(t.events, EVENT_SIZE * EVENT_CAPACITY);  // no seq of an earlier scenario
  const quiet = new Uint8Array(Math.max(n, 1));
  if (phase === 'scenario' && t.baseline !== null)
    t.baseline.forEach((count, i) => { quiet[i] = count > 0 ? 1 : 0; });
  t.quiet.writeByteArray(quiet.buffer);
  t.phase = phase;
  t.began = Date.now();
  t.beganMono = BigInt(t.now().toString());
  t.state.writeS32(PHASES[phase]);
  return true;
}

function readCounts(t) {
  const n = t.methods.length;
  return n === 0 ? new Uint32Array(0) : new Uint32Array(t.counts.readByteArray(4 * n));
}

async function callerTexts(addresses) {
  // ``module+0x…`` for native code, ``Namespace.Class:Method+0x…`` for JIT
  // code and for methods compiled ahead of time into a module (IL2CPP).
  const texts = addresses.map(address => {
    const module = Process.findModuleByAddress(address);
    return module === null ? null
      : engine.name(address) || `${module.name}+${address.sub(module.base)}`;
  });
  const jit = addresses.filter((_address, i) => texts[i] === null);
  let names = [];
  try {
    names = jit.length > 0 ? await engine.describeAll(jit) : [];
  } catch (_error) {
    // names stay unknown
  }
  let next = 0;
  return texts.map((text, i) => {
    if (text !== null)
      return text;
    return names[next++] || addresses[i].toString();
  });
}

async function readEvents(t) {
  // [[method index, thread, µs since the phase began, caller]] in call order.
  const written = t.state.add(4).readS32();
  const total = Math.min(written, EVENT_CAPACITY);
  const raw = [];
  if (total > 0) {
    const view = new DataView(t.events.readByteArray(total * EVENT_SIZE));
    for (let i = 0; i < total; i++) {
      const base = i * EVENT_SIZE;
      if (view.getUint32(base, true) !== i + 1)
        continue;
      raw.push([view.getUint32(base + 4, true), view.getUint32(base + 8, true),
                Number(view.getBigInt64(base + 24, true) - t.beganMono),
                view.getBigUint64(base + 16, true).toString(16)]);
    }
  }
  const callers = Array.from(new Set(raw.map(event => event[3])));
  const texts = await callerTexts(callers.map(caller => ptr('0x' + caller)));
  const names = new Map(callers.map((caller, i) => [caller, texts[i]]));
  return {
    events: raw.map(([method, thread, time, caller]) => [method, thread, time, names.get(caller)]),
    dropped: Math.max(0, written - EVENT_CAPACITY)
  };
}

async function finish() {
  const t = requireTrace();
  const phase = t.phase;
  if (phase === null)
    throw hermesError('error.trace.not_recording');
  t.state.writeS32(0);
  const duration = Date.now() - t.began;
  const counts = readCounts(t);
  const sparse = {};
  counts.forEach((count, i) => {
    if (count > 0)
      sparse[i] = count;
  });
  const result = { phase, duration, counts: sparse, events: [], dropped: 0 };
  if (phase === 'scenario')
    Object.assign(result, await readEvents(t));
  else
    t.baseline = counts;
  t.phase = null;
  return result;
}

function live() {
  // While recording: calls so far, how many methods, events written.
  if (trace === null || trace.phase === null)
    return;
  let calls = 0;
  let methods = 0;
  for (const count of readCounts(trace)) {
    calls += count;
    if (count > 0)
      methods++;
  }
  send({ kind: 'live', phase: trace.phase, calls, methods,
         events: Math.min(trace.state.add(4).readS32(), EVENT_CAPACITY) });
}

function stop() {
  if (trace === null)
    return false;
  const t = trace;
  trace = null;
  t.state.writeS32(0);
  const paused = pauseForHooking();
  try {
    for (const listener of t.listeners)
      listener.detach();
  } finally {
    resumeAfterHooking(paused);
  }
  engine.releaseCode();
  retired.push(t);
  updateUnmapWatch();
  return true;
}

// --- Freed code ---------------------------------------------------------------

let unmapWatch = null;

function tracesCodeIn(start, end) {
  // Whether a traced method starts in [start, end): binary search.
  const starts = trace.starts;
  let low = 0;
  let high = starts.length;
  while (low < high) {
    const middle = (low + high) >> 1;
    if (starts[middle].compare(start) < 0)
      low = middle + 1;
    else
      high = middle;
  }
  return low < starts.length && starts[low].compare(end) < 0;
}

function updateUnmapWatch() {
  if (trace !== null && unmapWatch === null) {
    unmapWatch = watchUnmaps((start, end) => {
      try {
        // Still mapped here: Frida can restore the code before it is gone.
        if (trace !== null && tracesCodeIn(start, end)) {
          stop();
          send({ kind: 'trace-ended' });
        }
      } catch (error) {
        send({ kind: 'agent-error', error: hermesMessage('error.trace.unmap',
            { error: String(error) }) });
      }
    });
  } else if (trace === null && unmapWatch !== null) {
    const watch = unmapWatch;
    unmapWatch = null;
    setTimeout(() => watch.detach(), 0);  // not from within its own callback
  }
}

function onCancel() {
  // A message rather than an RPC: it arrives while start() is still busy.
  cancelled = true;
  engine.cancelBatches();
  recv('cancel', onCancel);
}
recv('cancel', onCancel);

const liveTimer = setInterval(live, 500);
send({ kind: 'ready', engine: engine.refresh() ? engine.id : null });

rpc.exports = {
  assemblies() {
    return engine.assemblies();
  },
  classes(assembly) {
    return engine.classes(assembly);
  },
  choose,
  start,
  begin,
  finish,
  stop,
  async dispose() {
    clearInterval(liveTimer);
    cancelled = true;
    engine.cancelBatches();
    // The batch thread runs our C code: wait until it is out of it (it
    // checks after each method), but not forever should Mono hang.
    const deadline = Date.now() + DISPOSE_TIMEOUT;
    while ((engine.batchesRunning() || starting) && Date.now() < deadline)
      await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 20));
    stop();
    if (unmapWatch !== null) {
      unmapWatch.detach();
      unmapWatch = null;
    }
    Interceptor.flush();
    return true;
  }
};

```

`hermes/features/trace.py`:

```py
"""Trace: which C# methods a scenario in a game runs (e.g. Unity with Mono).

It works through the engine adapter of the game (see hermes/engines). While
it adds or removes its hooks, the game's threads are paused where the
platform needs it (Wine, see ``pauseThreads``).

The trace hooks many methods at once, e.g. all methods of the game's
assemblies, to find the one worth monitoring or hooking. It chooses them by
the catalog (see hermes.features.catalog_cache), so once the assemblies are
cached, listing and filtering them needs no reading in the game:

1. ``start`` compiles the chosen methods (like the method monitor does) and
   puts a Frida interceptor on each. The interceptors call a small C
   function (a Frida CModule) rather than JavaScript: it only counts the call
   and, while a scenario is recorded, notes method, thread, return address
   and time in a buffer. That keeps thousands of hooks affordable.
2. ``begin("baseline")`` … ``finish()`` records the noise: what the game
   calls anyway while one does nothing (Update methods, UI, AI …).
3. ``begin("scenario")`` … ``finish()`` records while one does the thing of
   interest in the game. Calls of methods seen in the baseline are only
   counted, not written into the call sequence.

``analyze`` then keeps the methods that are new in the scenario or ran
clearly more often than in the baseline, in the order they were first
called. Only the entry of a method is hooked, so Frida leaves return
addresses alone: exceptions pass through traced methods as usual.

Like the method monitor, the trace notices when Mono frees traced code
(Unity does so on exit) and removes all its interceptors first.
"""

import queue
import re
import threading
from dataclasses import dataclass

import frida
from PySide6.QtCore import QThread, Signal  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

from hermes.core import activity, logs, messages, settings
from hermes.core import sessions
from hermes.engines.registry import ENGINE_AGENT_SOURCE, resolve_engine
from hermes.features import catalog_cache, games
from hermes.features.assemblies import chosen_assemblies
from hermes.features.catalog import CatalogMethod
from hermes.attach.frida_attach import CLEANUP_ERRORS, FRIDA_ERRORS, attach_session
from hermes.agent.source import load_agent_source


# Calls of the scenario written into the sequence by default (setting
# trace_sequence); later ones are only counted.
EVENT_CAPACITY = 100_000

# A method ran "clearly more often" in the scenario than in the baseline when
# it ran this many times as often as expected, and at least MIN_EXTRA_CALLS
# times more.
MORE_FACTOR = 3.0
MIN_EXTRA_CALLS = 3

NEW, MORE, SAME = "new", "more", "same"

# Tokens per message choosing the methods: a message to Frida's gadget under
# Wine must stay below 128 KiB.
CHOOSE_PART = 4000

# ECMA-335 method flags, as the catalog has them
METHOD_ABSTRACT = 0x0400
METHOD_PINVOKE = 0x2000
IMPL_CODE_TYPE = 0x0003  # native or runtime (delegates) instead of IL
IMPL_INTERNAL_CALL = 0x1000
# ``Ns.List`1:Add``: a method of a generic class's definition
_GENERIC_CLASS = re.compile(r"`\d+:")

_AGENT_TEMPLATE = ENGINE_AGENT_SOURCE + load_agent_source(__file__)


def build_agent_source(event_capacity=EVENT_CAPACITY):
    return _AGENT_TEMPLATE.replace("EVENT_CAPACITY_VALUE", str(event_capacity))


def trace_methods(rows, engine="mono"):
    """CatalogMethods of the agent's ``start`` answer, in index order."""
    return [
        CatalogMethod(assembly, class_name, name, parameters, return_type, bool(static), token,
                      signature, engine)
        for assembly, class_name, name, parameters, return_type, static, token, signature in rows
    ]


def selection_parts(chosen):
    """``[[assembly, [token, ...]], ...]`` parts of ``[[assembly, token], ...]``.

    Each part holds at most CHOOSE_PART tokens; the agent's ``choose`` takes them.
    """
    parts, part, size = [], {}, 0
    for assembly, token in chosen:
        if size == CHOOSE_PART:
            parts.append([[name, tokens] for name, tokens in part.items()])
            part, size = {}, 0
        part.setdefault(assembly, []).append(token)
        size += 1
    if part:
        parts.append([[name, tokens] for name, tokens in part.items()])
    return parts


def untraceable(class_name, name, signature, flags, impl_flags):
    """Why a method cannot be traced (``"abstract"``, ``"native"``, ``"generic"``), else None."""
    if flags & METHOD_ABSTRACT:
        return "abstract"
    if flags & METHOD_PINVOKE or impl_flags & (IMPL_CODE_TYPE | IMPL_INTERNAL_CALL):
        return "native"
    # Open generics have no code of their own: List`1, Method<T>; Mono names
    # the class of a definition 'Ns.List<T>', its methods 'Ns.List`1:Add (T)'.
    head = signature.split(" (", 1)[0]
    if ("`" in class_name or _GENERIC_CLASS.search(head)
            or head[head.rfind(":") + 1:] != name):
        return "generic"
    return None


def select_methods(classes_of, words, engine="mono"):
    """The methods of ``classes_of`` matching ``words`` that a trace can hook.

    ``classes_of`` maps assemblies to their catalog ``classes`` answer (with
    the flags). Returns the CatalogMethods and how many matching methods
    cannot be traced: ``{abstract, native, generic}``.
    """
    words = [word.lower() for word in words]
    chosen = []
    skipped = {"abstract": 0, "native": 0, "generic": 0}
    for assembly, classes in classes_of.items():
        for class_name, methods in classes:
            for entry in methods:
                (name, parameters, return_type, static, token, signature, flags, impl_flags,
                 *names) = entry
                text = f"{class_name}:{name} {assembly}".lower()
                if not all(word in text for word in words):
                    continue
                reason = untraceable(class_name, name, signature, flags, impl_flags)
                if reason is not None:
                    skipped[reason] += 1
                else:
                    # Mono adds parameter names; older cache entries have none
                    chosen.append(CatalogMethod(assembly, class_name, name, parameters,
                                                return_type, bool(static), token, signature,
                                                engine, tuple(names[0]) if names else ()))
    return chosen, skipped


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TraceCall:
    """One call of the scenario."""

    method: int
    thread: int
    # microseconds since the scenario began
    time: int
    # where it was called from: ``Namespace.Class:Method+0x1a`` or ``module+0x…``
    caller: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TraceRow:
    """A method the scenario called, compared with the baseline."""

    method: int
    calls: int
    # calls per second in the scenario, and in the baseline (None: no baseline)
    rate: float
    baseline_rate: float | None
    verdict: str
    # position of its first call in the sequence (None: not in the sequence)
    first: int | None

    @property
    def notable(self):
        return self.verdict in (NEW, MORE)

    @property
    def factor(self):
        """How many times as often as in the baseline, or None."""
        if not self.baseline_rate:
            return None
        return self.rate / self.baseline_rate


def recorded_summary(result):
    """What a ``finish`` answer holds, in numbers, for the activity log."""
    counts = result.get("counts", {})
    summary = {"phase": result.get("phase"), "duration_ms": result.get("duration"),
               "functions": len(counts), "calls": sum(counts.values()),
               "events": len(result.get("events", [])), "dropped": result.get("dropped", 0)}
    for key in ("lost", "saturated", "waiting"):
        if result.get(key) is not None:
            summary[key] = result[key]
    return summary


def recording_calls(result):
    """TraceCalls of a ``finish`` answer of the scenario."""
    return [TraceCall(method, thread, time, caller or "")
            for method, thread, time, caller in result.get("events", [])]


def _counts(result):
    return {int(key): value for key, value in result.get("counts", {}).items()}


def analyze(scenario, baseline=None):
    """TraceRows of the methods ``scenario`` called (``finish`` answers).

    Without a baseline every method counts as new. Rows of methods in the
    call sequence come first, in the order they were first called; the
    others (only counted, since the baseline had them) follow, the most
    increased first.
    """
    seconds = max(scenario.get("duration", 0), 1) / 1000
    base_counts = _counts(baseline) if baseline else {}
    base_seconds = max(baseline.get("duration", 0), 1) / 1000 if baseline else None
    first = {}
    for position, (method, *_rest) in enumerate(scenario.get("events", [])):
        first.setdefault(method, position)
    rows = []
    for method, calls in _counts(scenario).items():
        base_calls = base_counts.get(method, 0)
        baseline_rate = None if baseline is None else base_calls / base_seconds
        if not base_calls:
            verdict = NEW
        else:
            expected = baseline_rate * seconds
            verdict = (MORE if calls >= MORE_FACTOR * expected
                       and calls - expected >= MIN_EXTRA_CALLS else SAME)
        rows.append(TraceRow(method, calls, calls / seconds, baseline_rate, verdict,
                             first.get(method)))
    rows.sort(key=lambda row: (
        row.first is None,
        row.first if row.first is not None else 0,
        {NEW: 0, MORE: 1, SAME: 2}[row.verdict],
        -(row.factor or 0),
        -row.calls,
    ))
    return rows


def calls_filter(text):
    """A test of call counts for ``text``, or None to keep every count.

    Alternatives are separated by commas: ``3`` exactly, ``3-10`` a range,
    ``>5``, ``>=5``, ``<5``, ``<=5`` bounds, ``%3`` multiples. A scenario
    repeated three times shows its functions with 3, 6, 9 … calls: ``%3``.
    Raises ValueError for text that is none of these.
    """
    tests = []
    for part in text.replace(" ", "").split(","):
        if not part:
            continue
        if part.startswith("%"):
            divisor = int(part[1:])
            if divisor <= 0:
                raise ValueError(part)
            tests.append(lambda calls, d=divisor: calls % d == 0)
        elif part.startswith((">=", "<=")):
            bound = int(part[2:])
            tests.append((lambda calls, b=bound: calls >= b) if part[0] == ">"
                         else (lambda calls, b=bound: calls <= b))
        elif part.startswith((">", "<")):
            bound = int(part[1:])
            tests.append((lambda calls, b=bound: calls > b) if part[0] == ">"
                         else (lambda calls, b=bound: calls < b))
        elif "-" in part:
            low, high = (int(value) for value in part.split("-", 1))
            tests.append(lambda calls, lo=low, hi=high: lo <= calls <= hi)
        else:
            exact = int(part)
            tests.append(lambda calls, e=exact: calls == e)
    if not tests:
        return None
    return lambda calls: any(test(calls) for test in tests)


class AgentWorker(QThread):
    """Keep a Frida session with one agent open and run commands on it.

    The base of the traces: the commands queue up from the GUI thread and run
    one after another as the agent's RPCs on the worker's thread (see
    ``_execute``); the agent's messages turn into signals (see ``_on_payload``).
    Subclasses decorate ``run`` with ``sessions.tracked`` and call
    ``_run_agent``.
    """

    # step, done, total, item at hand (e.g. the method Mono compiles)
    progress = Signal(str, int, int, str)
    # recording of the phase ("baseline", "scenario") has begun
    began = Signal(str)
    # {phase, calls, methods, events} while recording
    live = Signal(object)
    # a ``finish`` answer: {phase, duration, counts, events, dropped}
    recorded = Signal(object)
    stopped = Signal()
    # a command failed: what was asked, message
    command_failed = Signal(str, str)
    worker_failed = Signal(str)

    # What failed to load, for the log
    agent_name = "trace"
    # Its error messages: error.<agent_key>.load_timeout and .agent_failed
    agent_key = "trace"

    def __init__(self, pid, parent=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.pid = pid
        self._commands = queue.Queue()
        self._ready = threading.Event()
        self._agent_error = None
        self._detach_reason = None
        self._script = None
        self._session = None

    def agent_source(self):
        raise NotImplementedError

    def begin(self, phase):
        """Record ``"baseline"`` or ``"scenario"`` until ``finish``."""
        self._commands.put(("begin", phase))

    def finish(self):
        self._commands.put(("finish", None))

    def stop(self):
        """Remove the trace; the session stays open for another one."""
        self._commands.put(("stop", None))

    def cancel(self):
        """Stop preparing a trace as soon as possible.

        A message rather than a command: the worker is busy with the start
        until then.
        """
        script = self._script
        if script is not None:
            try:
                script.post({"type": "cancel"})
            except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                logs.cleanup_failed(error)

    def requestInterruption(self):  # pylint: disable=invalid-name
        self.cancel()
        super().requestInterruption()

    def _run_agent(self):
        session = None
        try:
            session = attach_session(self.pid)
            self._session = session
            sessions.SESSIONS.set_frida_session(self, session)
            session.on("detached", self._on_detached)
            self._load_script(session)
            while (not self.isInterruptionRequested() and self._detach_reason is None
                   and self._agent_error is None):
                try:
                    action, argument = self._commands.get(timeout=0.05)
                except queue.Empty:
                    continue
                if self._script is None:
                    break  # a fresh agent failed to load
                self._execute(self._script.exports_sync, action, argument)
            if self._agent_error and not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                raise RuntimeError(self._agent_error)
            if self._detach_reason and not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                raise messages.LocalizedRuntimeError("error.agent.detached",
                                                     reason=self._detach_reason)
        except FRIDA_ERRORS + (OSError, RuntimeError) as error:
            if not self.isInterruptionRequested():
                self.worker_failed.emit(messages.describe(error))
        finally:
            self._unload_script()
            if session is not None:
                try:
                    session.detach()
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)

    def _load_script(self, session):
        self._ready.clear()
        script = session.create_script(self.agent_source())
        script.on("message", self._on_message)
        script.load()
        self._script = script
        if not self._ready.wait(5):
            raise messages.LocalizedRuntimeError(f"error.{self.agent_key}.load_timeout")

    def _unload_script(self):
        script = self._script
        self._script = None
        if script is None:
            return
        try:
            script.exports_sync.dispose()
        except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
            logs.cleanup_failed(error)
        try:
            script.unload()
        except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
            logs.cleanup_failed(error)

    def _execute(self, api, action, argument):
        try:
            self._run_command(api, action, argument)
        except frida.RPCException as error:
            # Without the agent's stack trace
            self.command_failed.emit(action, messages.describe(error))

    def _run_command(self, api, action, argument):
        if action == "begin":
            api.begin(argument)
            self.began.emit(argument)
        elif action == "finish":
            result = api.finish()
            activity.record("trace_recorded", **recorded_summary(result))
            self.recorded.emit(result)
        elif action == "stop":
            api.stop()
            self.stopped.emit()

    def _on_message(self, message, _data):
        if message.get("type") == "error":
            self._agent_error = messages.describe(
                message.get("stack", messages.text(f"error.{self.agent_key}.agent_failed")))
            self._ready.set()
            return
        payload = message.get("payload", {})
        kind = payload.get("kind")
        if kind == "ready":
            self._ready.set()
        elif kind == "progress":
            self.progress.emit(payload.get("step", ""), payload.get("done", 0),
                               payload.get("total", 0), payload.get("current", ""))
        elif kind == "live":
            self.live.emit(payload)
        elif kind == "agent-error":
            logs.log.error("%s agent: %s", self.agent_name,
                           messages.describe(payload.get("error", "")))
        else:
            self._on_payload(kind, payload)

    def _on_payload(self, kind, payload):
        """A message of the agent the base does not know."""

    def _on_detached(self, reason, _crash):
        self._detach_reason = reason


class TraceWorker(AgentWorker):
    """Keep a Frida session open for a trace; see the module documentation.

    The public methods are safe to call from the GUI thread; results come
    back through the signals.
    """

    # {methods, skipped: {abstract, native, generic}, assemblies}
    planned = Signal(object)
    # every method a trace could hook (CatalogMethods), {abstract, native, generic}
    candidates_found = Signal(object, object)
    # CatalogMethods in index order, {skipped: {abstract, native, generic, com},
    # notCompiled, failed}
    started = Signal(object, object)
    # the game freed traced code (e.g. while exiting); the trace was removed
    ended = Signal()

    agent_name = "Mono trace"
    agent_key = "mono_trace"

    def __init__(self, pid, parent=None, engine=None, selection=()):
        super().__init__(pid, parent)
        self.engine = resolve_engine(pid, engine)
        # The user's assembly selection (see hermes.features.assemblies)
        self.selection = frozenset(selection)

    def set_selection(self, selection):
        """Trace only these assemblies from now on; none means all of the game."""
        self.selection = frozenset(selection)

    def agent_source(self):
        return build_agent_source(settings.get("trace_sequence"))

    def plan(self, words):
        """Count the methods a trace of ``words`` would hook; expect planned."""
        self._commands.put(("plan", list(words)))

    def trace(self, words):
        """Hook the methods of the game's assemblies matching ``words``."""
        self._commands.put(("start", list(words)))

    def candidates(self):
        """List every method a trace could hook; expect candidates_found."""
        self._commands.put(("candidates", []))

    def trace_selection(self, methods, words=()):
        """Hook exactly ``methods`` (CatalogMethods, e.g. from candidates_found).

        ``words`` (the free-text filter they were chosen with) only make the
        skipped methods count like ``trace`` counts them.
        """
        self._commands.put(("start", {"methods": [[m.assembly, m.token] for m in methods],
                                      "words": list(words)}))

    @sessions.tracked(sessions.TRACE)
    def run(self):
        self._run_agent()

    def _select(self, api, words):
        """The assemblies a trace covers, their traceable methods matching
        ``words`` and the count of the others (see select_methods).

        Assemblies come from the catalog cache, else from the agent.
        """
        found = api.assemblies()
        games.remember(self.pid, self.engine.id, found)
        mvids = {a["name"]: a.get("mvid") for a in found}
        names = chosen_assemblies(list(mvids), self.selection, self.engine)
        classes_of = {}
        for done, name in enumerate(names):
            self.progress.emit("catalog", done, len(names), name)
            classes_of[name] = catalog_cache.read_classes(
                self.engine.id, name, mvids[name], lambda name=name: api.classes(name))[0]
        self.progress.emit("catalog", len(names), len(names), "")
        return (names, *select_methods(classes_of, words, self.engine.id))

    def _run_command(self, api, action, argument):
        if action == "plan":
            names, methods, skipped = self._select(api, argument)
            self.planned.emit({"methods": len(methods), "skipped": skipped,
                               "assemblies": names})
        elif action == "candidates":
            _names, methods, skipped = self._select(api, argument)
            self.candidates_found.emit(methods, skipped)
        elif action == "start":
            # words, or {"methods": [[assembly, token], ...], "words": [...]}
            words = argument["words"] if isinstance(argument, dict) else argument
            _names, methods, skipped = self._select(api, words)
            chosen = (argument["methods"] if isinstance(argument, dict)
                      else [[method.assembly, method.token] for method in methods])
            for part in selection_parts(chosen):
                api.choose(part)
            answer = api.start({"skipped": skipped})
            self.started.emit(trace_methods(answer.pop("methods"), self.engine.id), answer)
        else:
            super()._run_command(api, action, argument)

    def _on_payload(self, kind, payload):
        if kind == "trace-ended":
            self.ended.emit()
```

`hermes/features/trace_filters.py`:

```py
"""Filters that pick the methods worth tracing from a game's catalog.

Tracing every method of a game is slow and, under Wine, unreliable: tens of
thousands of methods must be compiled and hooked. A filter picks a small set
from the catalog instead, deterministically, before anything is compiled:

``words``
    Any of them must match one of the name parts of the class or the method.
    Names are split at case changes, underscores, dots and digits (``HPBar``
    is ``hp`` + ``bar``). A word of up to four letters matches a part that is
    the word or its plural (``item``: ``Item``, ``Items``; not ``Itemize``),
    a longer word also the start of a part (``inventory``: ``InventorySlot``).
    ``gold`` matches ``AddGold`` and ``gold_amount`` but not ``Marigold``.
``exclude``
    None of them may match a name part (same rule).
``numbers``
    A parameter or the result must be a number (``int``, ``single``, ...).
``changes``
    The method must look like it changes a value: a property setter
    (``set_Gold``) or a name starting with a verb like ``Add``, ``Set`` or
    ``Spend``.

Several filters combine with OR. Compiler-generated code (lambdas, closures,
iterators: names with ``<``) is left out unless asked for: it is rarely what
one looks for and the source of most noise.
"""

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace
from functools import lru_cache

_NUMBERS = frozenset({
    "int", "uint", "long", "ulong", "short", "ushort", "byte", "sbyte",
    "single", "double", "float", "decimal",
})

CHANGE_VERBS = (
    "add", "remove", "set", "change", "modify", "increase", "decrease", "apply",
    "spend", "gain", "take", "give", "heal", "damage", "use", "consume", "reduce",
    "restore", "earn", "lose", "pay", "buy", "sell", "grant", "reward", "deduct",
    "subtract", "update", "inc", "dec",
)

# Camel case and acronyms: "HPBar" -> HP, Bar; "addGold2" -> add, Gold, 2
_PARTS = re.compile(r"[A-Z]+(?=[A-Z][a-z])|[A-Z]?[a-z]+|[A-Z]+|\d+")


def name_parts(text):
    """The lower-case parts of an identifier or a dotted name."""
    return list(_cached_parts(text))


# The names of a game repeat (classes have many methods, methods share names):
# what is known of a name or a part is worked out once. Filtering a catalog of
# 170,000 methods took seconds per filter without it.
@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def _cached_parts(text):
    return tuple(part.lower() for part in _PARTS.findall(text))


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def _method_parts(class_name, name):
    return _cached_parts(class_name) + _cached_parts(name)


def _parse_words(text):
    """Words of a user's filter: separated by spaces or commas, lower case."""
    return tuple(dict.fromkeys(word.lower() for word in re.split(r"[\s,;]+", text) if word))


def is_generated(method):
    """Whether the compiler made the method (lambda, closure, iterator, ...)."""
    return "<" in method.class_name or "<" in method.name


def has_number(method):
    """Whether a parameter or the result is a number."""
    return _has_number(method.parameters, method.return_type)


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def _has_number(parameters, return_type):
    types = re.split(r"[(),&\s]+", f"{parameters} {return_type}")
    return any(name in _NUMBERS for name in types)


def looks_like_change(method):
    """Whether the method's name says it changes a value."""
    return _looks_like_change(method.name)


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def _looks_like_change(name):
    if name.startswith("set_"):
        return True
    parts = _cached_parts(name)
    return bool(parts) and parts[0] in CHANGE_VERBS


SHORT_WORD = 4


def word_matches(word, part):
    """Whether a filter word matches one name part (see the module documentation)."""
    if part in (word, word + "s", word + "es"):
        return True
    return len(word) > SHORT_WORD and part.startswith(word)


@lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def _matches_part(words, part):
    return any(word_matches(word, part) for word in words)


def _matches_a_part(words, parts):
    return any(_matches_part(words, part) for part in parts)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TraceFilter:
    """One filter; see the module documentation."""

    name: str
    words: tuple = ()
    exclude: tuple = ()
    numbers: bool = False
    changes: bool = False
    # set for the filters hermes ships; they cannot be changed, only copied
    builtin: str = ""
    # database id of a user's filter
    filter_id: int = None
    description: str = field(default="", compare=False)

    def matches(self, method):
        """Whether ``method`` (a CatalogMethod) passes the filter."""
        parts = _method_parts(method.class_name, method.name)
        if self.words and not _matches_a_part(self.words, parts):
            return False
        if self.exclude and _matches_a_part(self.exclude, parts):
            return False
        if self.numbers and not has_number(method):
            return False
        if self.changes and not looks_like_change(method):
            return False
        return bool(self.words or self.numbers or self.changes)

    def to_json(self):
        """What the database keeps of a user's filter."""
        return {"words": list(self.words), "exclude": list(self.exclude),
                "numbers": self.numbers, "changes": self.changes}

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, name, data, filter_id=None, description=""):
        """A user's filter as the database keeps it."""
        return cls(name, tuple(data.get("words", ())), tuple(data.get("exclude", ())),
                   bool(data.get("numbers")), bool(data.get("changes")),
                   filter_id=filter_id, description=description)

    @classmethod
    def from_text(cls, name, words, exclude="", numbers=False, changes=False, **kwargs):
        """A filter from what a user typed (words separated by spaces or commas)."""
        return cls(name, _parse_words(words), _parse_words(exclude), numbers, changes,
                   **kwargs)

    def copy_as(self, name):
        """An editable copy (e.g. of a built-in filter)."""
        return replace(self, name=name, builtin="", filter_id=None)


# Platform and store code (achievements, leaderboards, cloud saves) uses
# the same words as game logic; the shipped filters leave it out.
PLATFORM_WORDS = ("sdk", "steam", "leaderboard", "galaxy", "achievement")

# Shipped filters; the names are translation keys ("trace.filter_<builtin>").
BUILTIN_FILTERS = (
    TraceFilter("money", ("gold", "money", "coin", "currency", "cash", "wallet", "price",
                          "cost", "wealth", "funds", "buy", "sell", "shop", "merchant"),
                PLATFORM_WORDS, builtin="money"),
    TraceFilter("inventory", ("inventory", "item", "slot", "stack", "pickup", "loot", "equip",
                              "bag", "stash", "quantity", "amount"),
                PLATFORM_WORDS, builtin="inventory"),
    TraceFilter("stats", ("health", "hp", "mana", "mp", "stamina", "endurance", "stat",
                          "attribute", "level", "xp", "experience", "skill", "ability",
                          "strength", "might", "resolve", "perception", "dexterity",
                          "intellect", "constitution", "luck"),
                PLATFORM_WORDS, builtin="stats"),
    TraceFilter("combat", ("damage", "attack", "hit", "heal", "armor", "armour", "defense",
                           "defence", "crit", "weapon", "kill", "death", "die", "wound",
                           "hurt", "resist"), PLATFORM_WORDS, builtin="combat"),
    TraceFilter("progress", ("quest", "variable", "flag", "progress", "objective", "journal",
                             "reputation"), PLATFORM_WORDS, builtin="progress"),
    TraceFilter("changes", exclude=PLATFORM_WORDS, numbers=True, changes=True,
                builtin="changes"),
)


def select_methods(methods, filters, words=(), generated=False):
    """The methods passing any of ``filters`` and all ``words``.

    Without filters every method passes them; ``words`` (lower case, as in
    the free-text filter) must all occur in ``Class:Method assembly``.
    Compiler-generated methods are left out unless ``generated``.
    """
    chosen = []
    for method in methods:
        if not generated and is_generated(method):
            continue
        if filters and not any(item.matches(method) for item in filters):
            continue
        if words:
            text = f"{method.class_name}:{method.name} {method.assembly}".lower()
            if not all(word in text for word in words):
                continue
        chosen.append(method)
    return chosen
```
