```py
    Only a hint: whether it really is one shows when the hook compiles it.
    """
    return _FUNCTION_START.match(source, _LEADING_COMMENTS.match(source).end()) is not None


class SyntaxChecker:
    """Check hook code in Frida's system session; see the module documentation.

    The session starts with the first check. Safe to use from several threads.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._session = None
        self._script = None
        self._failed = False
        # Lines the engine counts before the checked code, per kind
        self._offsets = {}

    @property
    def available(self):
        """Whether checks can run (the session started, or was not tried yet)."""
        return not self._failed

    def check(self, kind, code):
        """The SyntaxIssue of ``code`` (``FUNCTION`` or ``BODY``), else None.

        None too when the check cannot run.
        """
        with self._lock:
            if not self._start():
                return None
            try:
                answer = self._script.exports_sync.check(kind, code)
            except FRIDA_ERRORS + (frida.RPCException,) as error:
                logs.log.warning("syntax check failed: %s", error)
                return None
        if answer is None:
            return None
        _syntax, message, line = answer
        if line is not None:
            # A missing end shows on the line the check appends: the last one.
            line = min(max(1, line - self._offsets.get(kind, 0)), code.count("\n") + 1)
        return SyntaxIssue(message, line)

    def _start(self):
        if self._script is not None:
            return True
        if self._failed:
            return False
        try:
            session = frida.attach(0)
            script = session.create_script(_AGENT_SOURCE)
            script.load()
        except FRIDA_ERRORS + (frida.RPCException, OSError) as error:
            logs.log.warning("syntax check unavailable: %s", error)
            self._failed = True
            return False
        self._session, self._script = session, script
        # A syntax error on the first line tells how many lines come before.
        for kind in (FUNCTION, BODY):
            answer = script.exports_sync.check(kind, "@")
            line = answer[2] if answer is not None else None
            self._offsets[kind] = line - 1 if line is not None else 0
        return True

    def close(self):
        with self._lock:
            script, session = self._script, self._session
            self._script = self._session = None
        for close in (script and script.unload, session and session.detach):
            if close:
                try:
                    close()
                except CLEANUP_ERRORS as error:
                    logs.cleanup_failed(error)


_checker = None
_checker_lock = threading.Lock()


def checker():
    """The SyntaxChecker the program shares."""
    global _checker  # pylint: disable=global-statement
    with _checker_lock:
        if _checker is None:
            _checker = SyntaxChecker()
            atexit.register(_checker.close)
        return _checker


def check_function(source):
    """The SyntaxIssue of a template's source (a function expression), else None."""
    return checker().check(FUNCTION, source)


def check_body(code):
    """The SyntaxIssue of a ``code`` parameter (a function body), else None."""
    return checker().check(BODY, code)

```

`hermes/hooks/transforms.py`:

```py
"""Value transforms applied by write hooks inside the target process.

A transform is a JavaScript function expression that runs in the Frida agent
right after the hooked instruction has written the target value. It receives
a single ``ctx`` object and returns the value to store, or ``undefined`` /
``null`` to keep the value the game wrote:

    ctx.old        value before the write
    ctx.new        value the game just wrote
    ctx.delta      ctx.new - ctx.old
    ctx.params     the transform's JSON parameters (see ``ValueTransform.params``)
    ctx.state      per-hook object that persists between calls
    ctx.valueType  e.g. "int32", "uint8" or "float" (see hermes.core.value_types)
    ctx.address    target address as hex string
    ctx.writePc    address of the hooked write instruction as hex string
    ctx.threadId   id of the writing thread
    ctx.hookId     id of the hook
    ctx.log(...)   output shown in the hook debug window (no-op otherwise)

Integer results are truncated and clamped to the value type's range; int64
and uint64 values are passed as JavaScript numbers and are only exact up to
2**53.

New transforms subclass ``ValueTransform``, set ``kind`` and ``source`` and
register themselves with ``@register_transform``. Declaring ``parameters``
lets the UI build an input form for the transform automatically; labels
fall back to ``title`` / the parameter name.
``ScriptTransform`` accepts an arbitrary function source for one-off
experiments.

Hook templates maintained in the database are ``TransformDefinition``
objects (name, function source, parameters); ``TemplateTransform`` applies
one with concrete parameter values. Their ``kind`` is ``"value"`` for the
write hooks described above or ``"method"`` for method hooks, whose function
gets another ``ctx`` (see ``hermes.features.method_hooks``). A hook keeps its own copy of the
definition, so later template changes only reach it when they are adopted.
"""

import math
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from hermes.core.messages import LocalizedValueError


_TRANSFORMS = {}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TransformParameter:
    """Describes one constructor argument of a transform for UI forms.

    ``kind`` is ``"number"``, ``"choice"`` (one of ``choices``) or ``"code"``
    (multi-line text). ``optional`` parameters may be left empty (``None``).
    ``label`` and ``choice_labels`` (parallel to ``choices``) are display
    texts used by templates.
    """

    name: str
    kind: str = "number"
    default: object = None
    choices: tuple = ()
    optional: bool = False
    label: str = ""
    choice_labels: tuple = ()

    def choice_label(self, index):
        """Return the display text of ``choices[index]``."""
        if index < len(self.choice_labels) and self.choice_labels[index]:
            return self.choice_labels[index]
        return str(self.choices[index])

    def to_json(self):
        return {
            "name": self.name,
            "label": self.label,
            "kind": self.kind,
            "default": self.default,
            "optional": self.optional,
            "choices": [
                [choice, self.choice_label(index)]
                for index, choice in enumerate(self.choices)
            ],
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, data):
        choices = data.get("choices") or []
        return cls(
            name=data["name"],
            kind=data.get("kind", "number"),
            default=data.get("default"),
            choices=tuple(choice for choice, _label in choices),
            optional=bool(data.get("optional", False)),
            label=data.get("label", ""),
            choice_labels=tuple(label for _choice, label in choices),
        )


PARAMETER_NAME = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TransformDefinition:
    """A manipulation as maintained in a hook template or copied into a hook.

    Two definitions are equal when name, source and parameters match;
    ``description`` and ``template_id`` (the template it stems from) do not
    count.
    """

    name: str
    source: str
    parameters: tuple = ()
    description: str = field(default="", compare=False)
    template_id: int | None = field(default=None, compare=False)
    kind: str = "value"  # or "method"

    def parameters_json(self):
        return [parameter.to_json() for parameter in self.parameters]

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, name, source, parameters, description="", template_id=None,
                  kind="value"):
        # pylint: disable=too-many-arguments
        return cls(
            name=name,
            source=source,
            parameters=tuple(TransformParameter.from_json(p) for p in parameters or []),
            description=description or "",
            template_id=template_id,
            kind=kind or "value",
        )


def register_transform(cls):
    """Class decorator that makes a transform available via ``create_transform``."""
    if not cls.kind:
        raise ValueError(f"{cls.__name__} must define a non-empty kind")
    if cls.kind in _TRANSFORMS:
        raise ValueError(f"Transform kind already registered: {cls.kind}")
    _TRANSFORMS[cls.kind] = cls
    return cls


def available_transforms():
    """Return the registered transform classes keyed by kind."""
    return dict(_TRANSFORMS)


def create_transform(kind, **params):
    """Instantiate a registered transform by its kind."""
    try:
        cls = _TRANSFORMS[kind]
    except KeyError as error:
        raise LocalizedValueError("error.transforms.unknown_kind", kind=kind) from error
    return cls(**params)


def _require_number(name, value):
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        raise LocalizedValueError("error.transforms.not_number", name=name, value=repr(value))
    if not math.isfinite(value):
        raise LocalizedValueError("error.transforms.not_finite", name=name, value=repr(value))
    return value


class ValueTransform:
    """Base class for a value manipulation executed by the hook agent."""

    kind = ""
    title = ""
    source = ""
    parameters = ()

    def __init__(self, **params):
        self.params = self.validate(params)

    def form_values(self):
        """Return the constructor arguments, e.g. to pre-fill an edit form."""
        return dict(self.params)

    def validate(self, params):
        """Check and normalize the parameters; return the dict sent to the agent."""
        return params

    def to_agent(self):
        return {
            "kind": self.kind,
            "source": self.source,
            "params": self.params,
            "native": native_spec(self.source, self.params),
        }

    def describe(self):
        details = ", ".join(
            f"{key}={value}" for key, value in self.params.items() if value is not None
        )
        return f"{self.kind}({details})"

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<{type(self).__name__} {self.describe()}>"


@register_transform
class MultiplyTransform(ValueTransform):
    """Multiply the change of each write, e.g. gold gains x10."""

    kind = "multiply"
    title = "Multiply"
    source = r"""
function (ctx) {
  const { factor, direction } = ctx.params;
  if (direction === 'increase' && ctx.delta <= 0)
    return undefined;
  if (direction === 'decrease' && ctx.delta >= 0)
    return undefined;
  return ctx.old + ctx.delta * factor;
}
"""

    DIRECTIONS = ("increase", "decrease", "both")
    parameters = (
        TransformParameter("factor", default=2),
        TransformParameter("direction", "choice", "increase", DIRECTIONS),
    )

    def __init__(self, factor, direction="increase"):
        super().__init__(factor=factor, direction=direction)

    def validate(self, params):
        _require_number("factor", params["factor"])
        if params["direction"] not in self.DIRECTIONS:
            raise LocalizedValueError("error.transforms.choice", name="direction",
                                      choices=", ".join(self.DIRECTIONS))
        return params


@register_transform
class FreezeTransform(ValueTransform):
    """Overwrite every write with a fixed value."""

    kind = "freeze"
    title = "Freeze"
    source = r"""
function (ctx) {
  return ctx.params.value;
}
"""
    parameters = (TransformParameter("value", default=0),)

    def __init__(self, value):
        super().__init__(value=value)

    def validate(self, params):
        _require_number("value", params["value"])
        return params


@register_transform
class ClampTransform(ValueTransform):
    """Keep written values within optional lower and upper bounds."""

    kind = "clamp"
    title = "Clamp"
    parameters = (
        TransformParameter("minimum", optional=True),
        TransformParameter("maximum", optional=True),
    )
    source = r"""
function (ctx) {
  const { minimum, maximum } = ctx.params;
  let value = ctx.new;
  if (minimum !== null && value < minimum)
    value = minimum;
  if (maximum !== null && value > maximum)
    value = maximum;
  return value;
}
"""

    def __init__(self, minimum=None, maximum=None):
        super().__init__(minimum=minimum, maximum=maximum)

    def validate(self, params):
        minimum = params["minimum"]
        maximum = params["maximum"]
        if minimum is None and maximum is None:
            raise LocalizedValueError("error.transforms.clamp_bounds")
        if minimum is not None:
            _require_number("minimum", minimum)
        if maximum is not None:
            _require_number("maximum", maximum)
        if minimum is not None and maximum is not None and minimum > maximum:
            raise LocalizedValueError("error.transforms.clamp_order")
        return params


@register_transform
class ScriptTransform(ValueTransform):
    """User-supplied JavaScript function, e.g. ``ctx => ctx.old + ctx.delta * 2``."""

    kind = "script"
    title = "Script (JavaScript)"
    parameters = (
        TransformParameter(
            "source",
            "code",
            "ctx => ctx.delta > 0 ? ctx.old + ctx.delta * 2 : undefined",
        ),
    )

    def __init__(self, source, **params):
        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source.strip():
            raise LocalizedValueError("error.transforms.script_source")
        self.source = source
        super().__init__(**params)

    def form_values(self):
        return {"source": self.source, **self.params}

    def describe(self):
        first_line = self.source.strip().splitlines()[0]
        return f"script({first_line})"


class TemplateTransform(ValueTransform):
    """Apply a ``TransformDefinition`` with concrete parameter values."""

    kind = "template"

    def __init__(self, definition, **params):
        self.definition = definition
        self.source = definition.source
        self.parameters = definition.parameters
        super().__init__(**params)

    def validate(self, params):
        values = {}
        for parameter in self.parameters:
            value = params.get(parameter.name, parameter.default)
            name = parameter.label or parameter.name
            if value is None:
                if not parameter.optional and parameter.kind != "code":
                    raise LocalizedValueError("error.transforms.needs_value", name=name)
            elif parameter.kind == "number":
                _require_number(name, value)
            elif parameter.kind == "choice" and value not in parameter.choices:
                raise LocalizedValueError("error.transforms.choice", name=name,
                                          choices=", ".join(map(str, parameter.choices)))
            values[parameter.name] = value
        return values

    def to_agent(self):
        return {"kind": self.definition.name, "source": self.source, "params": self.params,
                "native": native_spec(self.source, self.params)}

    def describe(self):
        details = ", ".join(
            f"{key}={value}" for key, value in self.params.items() if value is not None
        )
        return f"{self.definition.name}({details})"


def _code(source):
    return " ".join(source.split())


def native_spec(source, params):
    """The built-in manipulation ``source`` is a copy of, for the agent to run in C.

    ``{"op": "multiply", "factor", "direction"}``, ``{"op": "freeze", "value"}``
    or ``{"op": "clamp", "minimum", "maximum"}``; None for other code (it runs
    in JavaScript). Copies of the examples in templates and imports count by
    their code, whatever their name.
    """
    code = _code(source)
    try:
        if code == _code(MultiplyTransform.source):
            return {"op": "multiply", "factor": float(params["factor"]),
                    "direction": params.get("direction", "increase")}
        if code == _code(FreezeTransform.source):
            return {"op": "freeze", "value": float(params["value"])}
        if code == _code(ClampTransform.source):
            minimum, maximum = params.get("minimum"), params.get("maximum")
            return {"op": "clamp",
                    "minimum": None if minimum is None else float(minimum),
                    "maximum": None if maximum is None else float(maximum)}
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    return None


def as_template_transform(transform):
    """Return ``transform`` as a TemplateTransform, e.g. to store its definition."""
    if isinstance(transform, TemplateTransform):
        return transform
    parameters = tuple(p for p in type(transform).parameters if p.name in transform.params)
    definition = TransformDefinition(transform.kind, transform.source.strip(), parameters)
    return TemplateTransform(definition, **transform.params)


# Built-in transforms offered as initial hook templates, keyed by seed key.
EXAMPLE_TEMPLATE_KINDS = ("multiply", "freeze", "clamp")


# Example templates for method hooks: seed key -> (source, parameters).
METHOD_EXAMPLES = {
    "method_multiply": (
        """function (ctx) {
  // The method's result times the factor, e.g. the damage of Health:DoDamage.
  return ctx.result * ctx.params.factor;
}""",
        (TransformParameter("factor", default=2),),
    ),
    "method_script": (
        """function (ctx) {
  // Runs the script typed into the hook's "script" field.
  if (ctx.state.code !== ctx.params.code) {
    ctx.state.code = ctx.params.code;
    ctx.state.fn = new Function('ctx', ctx.params.code);
  }
  return ctx.state.fn(ctx);
}""",
        (TransformParameter(
            "code", kind="code",
            default="""// ctx.phase ("before"/"after"), ctx.args.<name>, ctx.this, ctx.result, ctx.log(...)
// Objects: .name, .className, fields and properties directly (e.g. .IsPartyMember),
// .field("x"), .get("property"), .call("Method", ...), .component("Type")
// Static methods: ctx.call("Namespace.Class.Method", ...)
// After the call: return a value to replace the result, nothing to keep it.
// Before the call: ctx.args.x = …, obj.Field = … change what the method works with.
const attacker = ctx.args.attacker;
if (attacker && !/^(Player|Companion)_/.test(attacker.name))
  return ctx.result * 2;
"""),),
    ),
}


# Texts of the example templates. They are English whatever the language of
# the interface: templates are data, saved once and shared by exports.
EXAMPLE_TEXTS = {
    "multiply": "Multiplier",
    "multiply.factor": "Factor",
    "multiply.direction": "Apply to",
    "freeze": "Fixed value",
    "freeze.value": "Value",
    "clamp": "Clamp",
    "clamp.minimum": "Minimum",
    "clamp.maximum": "Maximum",
    "choice.increase": "Increases only",
    "choice.decrease": "Decreases only",
    "choice.both": "All changes",
    "method_multiply": "Result × factor",
    "method_multiply.factor": "Factor",
    "method_multiply.description":
        "Multiplies the method's result, e.g. the damage of Health:DoDamage.",
    "method_script": "Method script",
    "method_script.code": "Script",
    "method_script.description":
        "Your own JavaScript with ctx.args, ctx.this, ctx.result and ctx.call(…). After the "
        "call a returned value replaces the result, before the call assignments change "
        "arguments and fields (choose When above).",
}

# German texts earlier versions saved the examples with (keys as in
# EXAMPLE_TEXTS, ``<seed>.<parameter>_default`` for code). Only these are
# translated in saved templates and hooks; texts the user changed stay.
GERMAN_EXAMPLE_TEXTS = {
    "multiply": ("Multiplikator",),
    "multiply.factor": ("Faktor",),

    "freeze": ("Fester Wert",),

    "method_script.code": ("Skript",),
    "method_script.description": (

        "Aufruf ersetzt ein zurückgegebener Wert das Ergebnis, vor dem Aufruf ändern "

// Objekte: .name, .className, Felder und Eigenschaften direkt (z. B. .IsPartyMember),
// .field("x"), .get("Eigenschaft"), .call("Methode", ...), .component("Typ")
// Statische Methoden: ctx.call("Namespace.Klasse.Methode", ...)

  return ctx.result * 2;
""",

def example_templates():
    """Return the example template definitions ``{seed_key: definition}``."""
    def text(key, fallback):
        return EXAMPLE_TEXTS.get(key, fallback)

    examples = {}
    for kind in EXAMPLE_TEMPLATE_KINDS:
        cls = _TRANSFORMS[kind]
        parameters = tuple(
            TransformParameter(
                name=parameter.name,
                kind=parameter.kind,
                default=parameter.default,
                choices=parameter.choices,
                optional=parameter.optional,
                label=text(f"{kind}.{parameter.name}", parameter.name),
                choice_labels=tuple(
                    text(f"choice.{choice}", str(choice)) for choice in parameter.choices
                ),
            )
            for parameter in cls.parameters
        )
        examples[kind] = TransformDefinition(
            name=text(kind, cls.title or kind),
            source=cls.source.strip(),
            parameters=parameters,
            description=text(f"{kind}.description", ""),
        )
    for seed, (source, parameters) in METHOD_EXAMPLES.items():
        examples[seed] = TransformDefinition(
            name=text(seed, seed),
            source=source,
            parameters=tuple(
                TransformParameter(
                    name=parameter.name, kind=parameter.kind, default=parameter.default,
                    label=text(f"{seed}.{parameter.name}", parameter.name),
                )
                for parameter in parameters
            ),
            description=text(f"{seed}.description", ""),
            kind="method",
        )
    return examples


def example_seed(name):
    """The seed key of the example a German ``name`` was saved for, or None."""
    for seed in (*EXAMPLE_TEMPLATE_KINDS, *METHOD_EXAMPLES):
        if name in GERMAN_EXAMPLE_TEXTS.get(seed, ()):
            return seed
    return None


def english_example(seed, name, description, parameters):
    """``name``, ``description`` and ``parameters`` (JSON) of a saved example in English.

    Only the German texts of earlier versions are replaced: a name, label or
    script the user changed stays as it is.
    """
    english = example_templates()[seed]

    def swap(key, value, new):
        return new if value in GERMAN_EXAMPLE_TEXTS.get(key, ()) else value

    name = swap(seed, name, english.name)
    if not description or description in GERMAN_EXAMPLE_TEXTS.get(f"{seed}.description", ()):
        description = english.description or description
    by_name = {parameter.name: parameter for parameter in english.parameters}
    translated = []
    for parameter in parameters or []:
        parameter = dict(parameter)
        new = by_name.get(parameter.get("name"))
        if new is not None:
            key = f"{seed}.{new.name}"
            parameter["label"] = swap(key, parameter.get("label"), new.label)
            if new.kind == "code":
                parameter["default"] = swap(f"{key}_default", parameter.get("default"),
                                            new.default)
            parameter["choices"] = [
                [choice, swap(f"choice.{choice}", label, new.choice_label(new.choices.index(choice))
                              if choice in new.choices else label)]
                for choice, label in parameter.get("choices") or []
            ]
        translated.append(parameter)
    return name, description, translated
```

`hermes/main.py`:

```py
"""Application entry point for the Hermes Hook desktop application."""

import os
import signal
import sys

from PySide6.QtCore import QStandardPaths, QTimer  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module
from PySide6.QtGui import QIcon  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module
from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

from hermes.core import activity, logs, settings
from hermes.core.sessions import SESSIONS
from hermes.db.engine import init_db
from hermes.db.repository.settings import SettingsRepository
from hermes.ui.main_window import ICON_PATH, MainWindow
from hermes.ui.activity_recorder import UiRecorder
from hermes.ui.garbage import GarbageCollector
from hermes.ui.window_buttons import add_window_buttons
from hermes.ui.window_state import keep_window_state

DESKTOP_FILE_NAME = "hermes-hook"
WINDOWS_APP_ID = "hermes-hook.win"


def _set_windows_app_id():
    """Give the process an app ID of its own on Windows.

    The taskbar groups windows by program, here python.exe, and shows its
    icon. With an app ID of its own it shows the window icon instead. It has
    to be set before the first window opens.
    """
    if sys.platform != "win32":
        return
    import ctypes  # pylint: disable=import-outside-toplevel

    try:
        ctypes.WinDLL("shell32").SetCurrentProcessExplicitAppUserModelID(WINDOWS_APP_ID)
    except (AttributeError, OSError) as error:
        logs.log.warning("cannot set the Windows app ID: %s", error)


def start_activity_log():
    try:
        activity.setup()
    except OSError as error:
        logs.log.error("cannot write the activity log: %s", error)


def _follow_activity_setting(changed):
    # Switched on or off in the settings: at once, no restart needed.
    if "activity_log" not in changed:
        return
    if changed["activity_log"]:
        start_activity_log()
    else:
        activity.record("activity_log_off")
        activity.teardown()


def main() -> int:
    """Initialize the database and run the application event loop."""
    try:
        logs.setup()
    except OSError as error:
        print(f"Hermes cannot write its log: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
    logs.install_exception_hooks()
    init_db()
    settings.load(SettingsRepository().load())
    if settings.get("activity_log"):
        start_activity_log()
    settings.subscribe(_follow_activity_setting)

    _set_windows_app_id()
    app = QApplication(sys.argv)
    garbage_collector = GarbageCollector(app)
    garbage_collector.start()
    add_window_buttons(app)
    keep_window_state(app)
    app.setStyle("Fusion")
    app.setWindowIcon(QIcon(str(ICON_PATH)))
    # Wayland shows the icon of the app's .desktop file. Only name it when it
    # is installed; otherwise the desktop portal rejects the app ID with a warning.
    if QStandardPaths.locate(
        QStandardPaths.StandardLocation.ApplicationsLocation,
        f"{DESKTOP_FILE_NAME}.desktop",
    ):
        app.setDesktopFileName(DESKTOP_FILE_NAME)
    window = MainWindow(settings.language())
    recorder = UiRecorder(app)
    window.show()
    recorder.start()

    previous_sigint_handler = signal.getsignal(signal.SIGINT)
    signal.signal(
        signal.SIGINT,
        lambda _signum, _frame: QTimer.singleShot(0, window.close),
    )

    signal_check_timer = QTimer(app)
    signal_check_timer.setInterval(100)
    # Let Python process SIGINT while Qt's event loop is waiting in C++.
    signal_check_timer.timeout.connect(lambda: None)
    signal_check_timer.start()
    try:
        code = app.exec()
    finally:
        recorder.stop()
        signal_check_timer.stop()
        garbage_collector.stop()
        signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, previous_sigint_handler)
    logs.log.info("Hermes exits (code %s)", code)
    hanging = SESSIONS.sessions()
    activity.flush()
    activity.record("app_exited", code=code, hanging=[
        {"kind": session.kind, "pid": session.pid} for session in hanging],
        in_flight=activity.in_flight())
    activity.teardown()
    if hanging:
        logs.log.warning("exiting hard: %d session(s) did not end",
                         len(SESSIONS.sessions()))
        # A worker hangs in a call to the target (see ShutdownDialog). Python
        # would abort destroying its running QThread: leave without that.
        sys.stdout.flush()
        sys.stderr.flush()
        os._exit(code)  # pylint: disable=protected-access
    return code


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

`hermes/platform/__init__.py`:

```py
"""What differs between operating systems on hermes' side of a process.

Everything above this package reads and writes process memory, lists memory
regions and asks about processes through these names only:

``Mapping``
    A region of the address space (see mapping.py).
``read_mappings(pid)``
    The process' Mappings, sorted by address.
``ProcessMemory(pid, writable=False)``
    Context manager with ``read``, ``read_available``, ``read_pointer`` and
    ``write``.
``main_module(pid)``
    Module name of the program itself, or None.
``program_bits(pid)``
    32 or 64 for the program's executable, or None.
``process_start_time(pid)``
    A value that changes when the PID belongs to a new process; None once it
    has exited.
``is_wine_process(pid)``
    Whether the program runs under Wine or Proton.

Linux (linux.py) and Windows (windows.py) are implemented. wine.py reads
the PE images of a Wine process (``wine_program``, ``wine_bits``); like the
ptrace backends and the Wine gadget loader in ``hermes.attach`` it is
Linux-only at runtime.
"""

import sys

from hermes.platform.mapping import Mapping

if sys.platform.startswith("linux"):
    from hermes.platform.linux import (
        ProcessMemory,
        is_wine_process,
        main_module,
        process_start_time,
        program_bits,
        read_mappings,
    )
elif sys.platform == "win32":
    from hermes.platform.windows import (
        ProcessMemory,
        is_wine_process,
        main_module,
        process_start_time,
        program_bits,
        read_mappings,
    )
else:
    raise ImportError(f"hermes does not support {sys.platform} yet")

__all__ = [
    "Mapping",
    "ProcessMemory",
    "is_wine_process",
    "main_module",
    "process_start_time",
    "program_bits",
    "read_mappings",
]
```

`hermes/platform/linux.py`:

```py
"""Linux: processes through /proc/<pid>/maps, /proc/<pid>/mem and friends."""

import os
from pathlib import Path

from hermes.core.messages import LocalizedOSError
from hermes.platform.mapping import Mapping

# Kernel mappings that are no memory of the program.
_KERNEL_MAPPINGS = {"[vvar]", "[vvar_vclock]", "[vsyscall]", "[vdso]"}


def parse_maps(lines):
    """Parse the lines of /proc/<pid>/maps into Mappings.

    A module is a file with executable code. All its mappings belong to it,
    and so does an anonymous writable mapping right behind one of them (.bss,
    if it does not fit the file). Other mapped files, e.g.
    /dev/dri/renderD128 or game assets, are no modules; Frida does not know
    them either.
    """
    regions = []
    for line in lines:
        fields = line.split(maxsplit=5)
        if len(fields) < 5:
            continue
        start, end = (int(bound, 16) for bound in fields[0].split("-"))
        path = fields[5].strip() if len(fields) == 6 else ""
        regions.append((start, end, fields[1], path))
    modules = {
        path for _start, _end, permissions, path in regions
        if path.startswith("/") and "x" in permissions
    }
    mappings = []
    previous = None
    for start, end, permissions, path in sorted(regions):
        writable = (
            all(flag in permissions for flag in "rwp")
            and not path.startswith("/dev/") and path not in _KERNEL_MAPPINGS
        )
        module = None
        if path in modules:
            module = os.path.basename(path)
        elif writable and not path and previous is not None \
                and previous.path in modules and previous.end == start:
            module = previous.module
        previous = Mapping(start, end, permissions, path, module, writable)
        mappings.append(previous)
    return mappings


def read_mappings(pid):
    """Return the Mappings of process ``pid``."""
    with open(f"/proc/{pid}/maps", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as maps_file:
        return parse_maps(maps_file)


def main_module(pid):
    """Return the module name of the program itself, or None if unknown."""
    try:
        path = os.readlink(f"/proc/{pid}/exe")
    except OSError:
        return None
    return os.path.basename(path.removesuffix(" (deleted)"))


class ProcessMemory:
    """Read, and if ``writable`` also write, a process' memory via /proc/<pid>/mem."""

    def __init__(self, pid, writable=False):
        self.pid = pid
        self._file = open(  # pylint: disable=consider-using-with
            f"/proc/{pid}/mem", "r+b" if writable else "rb", buffering=0
        )

    def close(self):
        """Close the memory file."""
        self._file.__exit__(None, None, None)

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *_exc):
        self.close()

    def read_available(self, address, size):
        """Return up to ``size`` bytes at ``address``.

        Fewer if readable memory ends earlier, ``b""`` if ``address`` itself
        cannot be read.
        """
        if address < 0:
            return b""
        try:
            self._file.seek(address)
            return self._file.read(size)
        except (OSError, OverflowError, ValueError):
            return b""

    def read(self, address, size):
        """Return ``size`` bytes or None if the memory cannot be read."""
        data = self.read_available(address, size)
        return data if len(data) == size else None

    def read_pointer(self, address, size=8):
        """Return the pointer at ``address`` or None."""
        data = self.read(address, size)
        return None if data is None else int.from_bytes(data, "little")

    def write(self, address, data):
        """Write ``data`` to ``address``; raises OSError unless all of it was written.

        Read-only pages are written too: the kernel writes through them.
        """
        self._file.seek(address)
        written = self._file.write(data)
        if written != len(data):
            raise LocalizedOSError("error.platform.incomplete_write_linux", written=written,
                                   size=len(data))


def process_start_time(pid, proc_root="/proc"):
    """Return when ``pid`` was started (clock ticks after boot), or None.

    None means the process has exited, including zombies that wait for their
    parent. Comparing start times tells a restarted program that got the same
    PID apart from the original one.
    """
    try:
        stat = (Path(proc_root) / str(pid) / "stat").read_text()
    except OSError:
        return None
    # The command name may contain spaces and parentheses; fields follow the
    # last ')'. They start with field 3 (state); starttime is field 22.
    fields = stat[stat.rindex(")") + 2:].split()
    if fields[0] in {"Z", "X", "x"}:
        return None
    return int(fields[19])


def program_bits(pid, proc_root="/proc"):
    """Return 32 or 64 for the ELF program ``pid`` runs, or None if unknown.

    Under Wine that is the loader's; the Windows program's own is
    ``wine_bits`` (hermes.platform.wine).
    """
    try:
        with open(f"{proc_root}/{pid}/exe", "rb") as exe:
            ident = exe.read(5)
    except OSError:
        return None
    if ident[:4] != b"\x7fELF":
        return None
    # EI_CLASS: ELFCLASS32 or ELFCLASS64
    return {1: 32, 2: 64}.get(ident[4])


def is_wine_process(pid, proc_root="/proc"):
    """Return True if ``pid`` runs under Wine or Proton.

    Wine starts Windows programs through its static ``wine-preloader``
    (``wine64-preloader``), or through the ``wine`` loader itself.
    """
    try:
        name = (Path(proc_root) / str(pid) / "exe").readlink().name
    except OSError:
        return False
    return name in {"wine", "wine64"} or (
        name.startswith("wine") and name.endswith("-preloader"))
```

`hermes/platform/mapping.py`:

```py
"""The address-space region every platform reports."""

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Mapping:
    """A region of a process' address space.

    The platform layer decides what the fields mean for its system, so code
    above it needs no knowledge of /proc or Windows memory APIs.
    """

    start: int
    end: int
    # Shown to the user, e.g. "rw-p".
    permissions: str
    # Backing file or a name such as "[heap]"; "" for anonymous memory.
    path: str = ""
    # Name of the loaded module (program or library) the region belongs to,
    # its data and .bss included; None for other memory.
    module: str | None = None
    # Private, readable and writable memory: where values and pointers live.
    writable: bool = False

```

```py
"""Windows: processes through the Win32 API (ReadProcessMemory, VirtualQueryEx, …).

Modules are the PE images the process' loader lists, under the names the
loader gives them (``KERNEL32.DLL``); Frida's Windows backend uses the same
names, so ``module+offset`` from here and from an agent agree.

``proc_root`` parameters exist only to match the Linux signatures and are
ignored.

from contextlib import contextmanager

    PAGE_NOACCESS: "---",
    PAGE_READONLY: "r--",
    PAGE_READWRITE: "rw-",
    PAGE_WRITECOPY: "rw-",
    PAGE_EXECUTE: "--x",

    PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE: "rwx",
    PAGE_EXECUTE_WRITECOPY: "rwx",
}

class _MemoryBasicInformation(ctypes.Structure):

        ("BaseAddress", ctypes.c_void_p),

    function = getattr(_kernel32, name)
    function.restype = restype
    function.argtypes = argtypes
    return function

    # Windows 10 1607 and later.
    _GetThreadDescription = _function(
        "GetThreadDescription", ctypes.c_long, wintypes.HANDLE, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_void_p))
except AttributeError:
    _GetThreadDescription = None


def _open(pid, access):
    """Return a handle to ``pid``; raises OSError (PermissionError if denied)."""
    handle = _OpenProcess(access, False, pid)
    if not handle:
        raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())
    return handle


@contextmanager
def _process(pid, access):
    handle = _open(pid, access)
    try:
        yield handle
    finally:
        _CloseHandle(handle)


def _regions(handle, address=0):
    """Yield the MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION of each region from ``address`` on."""
    while address < _ADDRESS_LIMIT:
        info = _MemoryBasicInformation()
        if not _VirtualQueryEx(handle, ctypes.c_void_p(address), ctypes.byref(info),
                               ctypes.sizeof(info)):
            return
        yield info
        address = (info.BaseAddress or 0) + info.RegionSize


def _readable(info):
    return (info.State == MEM_COMMIT and not info.Protect & PAGE_GUARD
            and info.Protect & 0xFF not in (PAGE_NOACCESS, PAGE_EXECUTE))


def _modules(handle):
    """{load address: (loader name, path)} of the loaded PE images."""
    needed = wintypes.DWORD()
    count = 1024
    while True:
        bases = (ctypes.c_void_p * count)()
        if not _EnumProcessModulesEx(handle, bases, ctypes.sizeof(bases), ctypes.byref(needed),
                                     LIST_MODULES_ALL):
            return {}
        if needed.value <= ctypes.sizeof(bases):
            break
        count = needed.value // ctypes.sizeof(ctypes.c_void_p) + 64
    modules = {}
    buffer = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(32768)
    for base in bases[:needed.value // ctypes.sizeof(ctypes.c_void_p)]:
        if not base:
            continue
        if not _GetModuleBaseNameW(handle, base, buffer, len(buffer)):
            continue
        name = buffer.value
        path = buffer.value if _GetModuleFileNameExW(handle, base, buffer, len(buffer)) else name
        modules[base] = (name, path)
    return modules


_dos_devices = None


def _dos_path(device_path):
    r"""``\Device\HarddiskVolume3\x`` as ``C:\x``; unchanged if no drive matches."""
    global _dos_devices  # pylint: disable=global-statement
    if _dos_devices is None:
        _dos_devices = {}
        buffer = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(1024)
        for letter in string.ascii_uppercase:
            if _QueryDosDeviceW(f"{letter}:", buffer, len(buffer)):
                _dos_devices[buffer.value + "\\"] = f"{letter}:\\"
    for device, drive in _dos_devices.items():
        if device_path.startswith(device):
            return drive + device_path[len(device):]
    return device_path


def _mapped_file(handle, address):
    buffer = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(32768)
    if not _GetMappedFileNameW(handle, ctypes.c_void_p(address), buffer, len(buffer)):
        return ""
    return _dos_path(buffer.value)


def read_mappings(pid):
    """Return the Mappings of process ``pid``: its committed memory regions."""
    with _process(pid, PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION | PROCESS_VM_READ) as handle:
        modules = _modules(handle)
        files = {}
        mappings = []
        for info in _regions(handle):
            if info.State != MEM_COMMIT:
                continue
            start = info.BaseAddress or 0
            allocation = info.AllocationBase or 0
            protection = info.Protect & 0xFF
            shared = info.Type == MEM_MAPPED and protection in _SHARED_WRITABLE
            permissions = _PERMISSIONS.get(protection, "---") + ("s" if shared else "p")
            if info.Protect & PAGE_GUARD:
                permissions = "---p"
            writable = (
                permissions.startswith("rw") and not shared
                and not info.Protect & (PAGE_GUARD | PAGE_NOCACHE | PAGE_WRITECOMBINE)
            )
            module = None
            path = ""
            if info.Type == MEM_IMAGE:
                if allocation in modules:
                    module, path = modules[allocation]
                else:
                    # Not (yet) in the loader's list: name it after its file.
                    if allocation not in files:
                        files[allocation] = _mapped_file(handle, allocation)
                    path = files[allocation]
                    module = ntpath.basename(path) or None
            elif info.Type == MEM_MAPPED:
                if allocation not in files:
                    files[allocation] = _mapped_file(handle, allocation)
                path = files[allocation]
            mappings.append(Mapping(start, start + info.RegionSize, permissions, path, module,
                                    writable))
        return mappings


def _image_path(pid):
    with _process(pid, PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) as handle:
        buffer = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(32768)
        size = wintypes.DWORD(len(buffer))
        if not _QueryFullProcessImageNameW(handle, 0, buffer, ctypes.byref(size)):
            raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())
        return buffer.value


def main_module(pid):
    """Return the module name of the program itself, or None if unknown."""
    try:
        return ntpath.basename(_image_path(pid))
    except OSError:
        return None


class ProcessMemory:
    """Read, and if ``writable`` also write, a process' memory via ReadProcessMemory."""

    def __init__(self, pid, writable=False):
        self.pid = pid
        access = PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION | PROCESS_VM_READ
        if writable:
            access |= PROCESS_VM_WRITE | PROCESS_VM_OPERATION
        self._handle = _open(pid, access)

    def close(self):
        """Close the process handle."""
        if self._handle:
            _CloseHandle(self._handle)
            self._handle = None

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *_exc):
        self.close()

    def _read(self, address, size):
        buffer = ctypes.create_string_buffer(size)
        done = ctypes.c_size_t()
        if not _ReadProcessMemory(self._handle, ctypes.c_void_p(address), buffer, size,
                                  ctypes.byref(done)) or done.value != size:
            return None
        return buffer.raw

    def _readable_size(self, address, size):
        """How many of ``size`` bytes at ``address`` lie in readable memory."""
        end = address
        for info in _regions(self._handle, address):
            if not _readable(info):
                break
            end = (info.BaseAddress or 0) + info.RegionSize
            if end >= address + size:
                return size
        return max(0, end - address)

    def read_available(self, address, size):
        """Return up to ``size`` bytes at ``address``.

        Fewer if readable memory ends earlier, ``b""`` if ``address`` itself
        cannot be read.
        """
        if address < 0 or size <= 0 or address + size > _ADDRESS_LIMIT:
            return b""
        data = self._read(address, size)
        if data is not None:
            return data
        # ReadProcessMemory reads all or nothing: retry up to the readable end.
        readable = self._readable_size(address, size)
        if readable <= 0 or readable >= size:
            return b""
        return self._read(address, readable) or b""

    def read(self, address, size):
        """Return ``size`` bytes or None if the memory cannot be read."""
        data = self.read_available(address, size)
        return data if len(data) == size else None

    def read_pointer(self, address, size=8):
        """Return the pointer at ``address`` or None."""
        data = self.read(address, size)
        return None if data is None else int.from_bytes(data, "little")

    def _write(self, address, data):
        done = ctypes.c_size_t()
        return bool(_WriteProcessMemory(self._handle, ctypes.c_void_p(address), data, len(data),
                                        ctypes.byref(done))) and done.value == len(data)

    def write(self, address, data):
        """Write ``data`` to ``address``; raises OSError unless all of it was written.

        Read-only pages are written too, as on Linux: their protection is
        lifted for the write and restored afterwards.
        """
        data = bytes(data)
        if self._write(address, data):
            return
        end = address + len(data)
        restore = []
        try:
            for info in _regions(self._handle, address):
                start = info.BaseAddress or 0
                if start >= end:
                    break
                protection = info.Protect & 0xFF
                writable = (PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE if protection in _EXECUTABLE
                            else PAGE_READWRITE)
                old = wintypes.DWORD()
                low, high = max(start, address), min(start + info.RegionSize, end)
                if not _VirtualProtectEx(self._handle, ctypes.c_void_p(low), high - low, writable,
                                         ctypes.byref(old)):
                    raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())
                restore.append((low, high - low, old.value))
            written = self._write(address, data)
        finally:
            for low, size, protection in restore:
                _VirtualProtectEx(self._handle, ctypes.c_void_p(low), size, protection,
                                  ctypes.byref(wintypes.DWORD()))
        _FlushInstructionCache(self._handle, ctypes.c_void_p(address), len(data))
        if not written:
            raise LocalizedOSError("error.platform.incomplete_write_windows", size=len(data),
                                   address=f"{address:#x}")


def process_start_time(pid, proc_root=None):  # pylint: disable=unused-argument
    """Return when ``pid`` was started (FILETIME), or None once it has exited.

    Comparing start times tells a restarted program that got the same PID
    apart from the original one.
    """
    try:
        with _process(pid, PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION | SYNCHRONIZE) as handle:
            if _WaitForSingleObject(handle, 0) != STILL_RUNNING:
                return None
            times = [ctypes.c_uint64() for _ in range(4)]
            if not _GetProcessTimes(handle, *(ctypes.byref(time) for time in times)):
                return None
            return times[0].value
    except OSError:
        return None


def program_bits(pid, proc_root=None):  # pylint: disable=unused-argument
    """Return 32 or 64 for the program ``pid`` runs, or None if unknown."""
    try:
        with _process(pid, PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) as handle:
            if _IsWow64Process2 is not None:
                process_machine, native_machine = wintypes.USHORT(), wintypes.USHORT()
                if not _IsWow64Process2(handle, ctypes.byref(process_machine),
                                        ctypes.byref(native_machine)):
                    return None
                machine = process_machine.value
                if machine == IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_UNKNOWN:
                    machine = native_machine.value
                return 32 if machine in _32BIT_MACHINES else 64
            wow64 = wintypes.BOOL()
            if not _IsWow64Process(handle, ctypes.byref(wow64)):
                return None
            return 32 if wow64.value else 64
    except OSError:
        return None


def is_wine_process(pid, proc_root=None):  # pylint: disable=unused-argument
    """Always False: on Windows a program runs natively."""
    return False


@contextmanager
def _thread(tid):
    handle = _OpenThread(THREAD_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, False, tid)
    if not handle:
        raise ctypes.WinError(ctypes.get_last_error())
    try:
        yield handle
    finally:
        _CloseHandle(handle)


def thread_times(tid):
    """(CPU seconds, CPU cycles) thread ``tid`` has used, or None once it is gone.

    The cycles tell a thread that woke up only briefly from one that slept,
    below the resolution of the CPU time.
    """
    try:
        with _thread(tid) as handle:
            times = [ctypes.c_uint64() for _ in range(4)]
            cycles = ctypes.c_uint64()
            if not _GetThreadTimes(handle, *(ctypes.byref(time) for time in times)) \
                    or not _QueryThreadCycleTime(handle, ctypes.byref(cycles)):
                return None
    except OSError:
        return None
    # Kernel and user time, in units of 100 ns.
    return (times[2].value + times[3].value) / 10_000_000, cycles.value


def thread_name(tid):
    """The name a program gave thread ``tid`` (SetThreadDescription), or None."""
    if _GetThreadDescription is None:
        return None
    try:
        with _thread(tid) as handle:
            text = ctypes.c_void_p()
            if _GetThreadDescription(handle, ctypes.byref(text)) < 0 or not text.value:
                return None
            try:
                return ctypes.wstring_at(text.value) or None
            finally:
                _LocalFree(text)
    except OSError:
        return None

```

`hermes/platform/wine.py`:

```py
"""Wine/Proton programs seen from outside: the PE images a Wine process maps.

Linux only at runtime (it reads /proc/<pid>/maps and /proc/<pid>/mem); on
Windows no program runs under Wine, so nobody calls it there.
"""

import os
import struct
from dataclasses import dataclass

_MACHINE_I386 = 0x14C


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PeImage:
    """A PE file mapped into a Wine process."""

    name: str
    path: str
    base: int
    machine: int

    @property
    def bits(self):
        """32 or 64."""
        return 32 if self.machine == _MACHINE_I386 else 64


class RawMemory:
    """Read and write another process's memory through /proc/<pid>/mem."""

    def __init__(self, pid, writable=True):
        self._fd = os.open(f"/proc/{pid}/mem", os.O_RDWR if writable else os.O_RDONLY)

    def close(self):
        """Close the file."""
        os.close(self._fd)

    def read(self, address, size):
        """Read ``size`` bytes."""
        return os.pread(self._fd, size, address)

    def write(self, address, data):
        """Write ``data`` (ptrace access reaches read-only pages too)."""
        os.pwrite(self._fd, data, address)

    def u16(self, address):
        """Read a little-endian unsigned 16-bit value."""
        return struct.unpack("<H", self.read(address, 2))[0]

    def u32(self, address):
        """Read a little-endian unsigned 32-bit value."""
        return struct.unpack("<I", self.read(address, 4))[0]

    def cstr(self, address, limit=256):
        """Read a NUL-terminated ASCII string."""
        raw = self.read(address, limit)
        return raw.split(b"\0", 1)[0].decode("latin-1")


def _maps(pid):
    """Yield ``(start, end, permissions, offset, path)`` per mapping."""
    with open(f"/proc/{pid}/maps", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as maps:
        for line in maps:
            fields = line.split(maxsplit=5)
            if len(fields) < 5:
                continue
            start, end = (int(bound, 16) for bound in fields[0].split("-"))
            path = fields[5].strip() if len(fields) == 6 else ""
            yield start, end, fields[1], int(fields[2], 16), path


def pe_images(pid, memory):
    """Return the PE images (DLLs and EXEs) mapped into ``pid``.

    Wine's PE modules are not reported by Frida's module list, so hermes finds
    them by walking /proc/<pid>/maps for file-backed ranges that begin with an
    ``MZ``/``PE`` header at file offset 0.
    """
    images = []
    for start, _end, _perms, offset, path in _maps(pid):
        if offset or not path.lower().endswith((".dll", ".exe")):
            continue
        try:
            if memory.read(start, 2) != b"MZ":
                continue
            header = start + memory.u32(start + 0x3C)
            if memory.read(header, 4) != b"PE\0\0":
                continue
            machine = memory.u16(header + 4)
        except OSError:
            continue
        images.append(PeImage(os.path.basename(path).lower(), path, start, machine))
    return images


def wine_program(pid):
    """(path, 32 or 64) of the Windows program a Wine process runs, or (None, None)."""
    try:
        memory = RawMemory(pid, writable=False)
    except OSError:
        return None, None
    try:
        images = pe_images(pid, memory)
    finally:
        memory.close()
    main = next((image for image in images if image.name.endswith(".exe")), None)
    return (main.path, main.bits) if main else (None, None)


def wine_bits(pid):
    """Return 32 or 64 for the program a Wine process runs, or None if unknown."""
    return wine_program(pid)[1]


def pe_export(memory, image, name):
    """Resolve an exported function of ``image`` to its address, or None."""
    base = image.base
    header = base + memory.u32(base + 0x3C)
    optional = header + 24
    magic = memory.u16(optional)
    # The export directory RVA sits in data directory 0, whose offset into the
    # optional header differs between PE32 (96) and PE32+ (112).
    directory = optional + (112 if magic == 0x20B else 96)
    export = base + memory.u32(directory)
    count = memory.u32(export + 24)
    functions = base + memory.u32(export + 28)
    names = base + memory.u32(export + 32)
    ordinals = base + memory.u32(export + 36)
    target = name.encode("latin-1")
    for index in range(count):
        entry = base + memory.u32(names + index * 4)
        if memory.cstr(entry, len(target) + 1).encode("latin-1") == target:
            ordinal = memory.u16(ordinals + index * 2)
            return base + memory.u32(functions + ordinal * 4)
    return None

```

`hermes/ui/activity_recorder.py`:

```py
"""Record what is clicked in Hermes into the activity log (hermes.core.activity).

``UiRecorder`` needs no change to the windows: every ``SCAN_INTERVAL_MS`` it
connects to the buttons, menu actions, combo boxes, tab bars and item views
that appeared since, and notes the windows and dialogs that opened or
closed. Only what was clicked is recorded, with its window; nothing typed
into fields.

Not an event filter on the application: Python event filters can receive
wrappers for Qt objects that are being deleted; accessing those wrappers
crashed Hermes in the Qt binding's object wrapper.
"""

from PySide6.QtCore import QObject, Qt, QTimer  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module
from PySide6.QtWidgets import (  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module
    QAbstractButton,
    QAbstractItemView,
    QApplication,
    QComboBox,
    QTabBar,
    QToolButton,
)

from hermes.core import activity, logs


SCAN_INTERVAL_MS = 500
_MARK = "_hermes_recorded"
_PRESSED = "_hermes_pressed_text"
_WINDOWS = (Qt.WindowType.Window, Qt.WindowType.Dialog)


def _text(text):
    return text.replace("&&", "\0").replace("&", "").replace("\0", "&").strip()


def _window(widget):
    window = widget.window()
    return {"window": window.windowTitle() or type(window).__name__}


def _name(widget):
    # The object name tells widgets of the same text apart; Qt's own are "qt_…"
    name = widget.objectName()
    return {"name": name} if name and not name.startswith("qt_") else {}


class UiRecorder(QObject):
    """See the module documentation; ``start`` it, ``stop`` it before the windows go."""

    def __init__(self, parent=None, interval_ms=SCAN_INTERVAL_MS):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self._timer = QTimer(self)
        self._timer.setInterval(interval_ms)
        self._timer.timeout.connect(self.scan)
        # id of a shown window -> (title, class name)
        self._shown = {}

    def start(self):
        self.scan()
        self._timer.start()

    def stop(self):
        self._timer.stop()

    def scan(self):
        """Connect to what appeared, note the windows that opened or closed."""
        try:
            for widget in QApplication.allWidgets():
                self._connect(widget)
                for action in widget.actions():
                    self._connect_action(action)
            self._windows()
        except Exception as error:  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
            # Recording must never get in the way of the window.
            logs.cleanup_failed(error)

    def _windows(self):
        shown = {}
        for widget in QApplication.topLevelWidgets():
            if widget.isVisible() and widget.windowType() in _WINDOWS:
                shown[id(widget)] = (widget.windowTitle(), type(widget).__name__)
        for key, (title, kind) in shown.items():
            if key not in self._shown:
                activity.record("window_shown", window=title, widget=kind)
        for key, (title, kind) in self._shown.items():
            if key not in shown:
                activity.record("window_hidden", window=title, widget=kind)
        self._shown = shown

    @staticmethod
    def _marked(item):
        if item.property(_MARK):
            return True
        item.setProperty(_MARK, True)
        return False

    def _connect(self, widget):
        if isinstance(widget, QAbstractButton):
            # A tool button showing an action: the action records the click.
            if isinstance(widget, QToolButton) and widget.defaultAction() is not None:
                return
            if not self._marked(widget):
                # The text before the click: the window's own slot may change it first.
                widget.pressed.connect(
                    lambda button=widget: button.setProperty(_PRESSED, _text(button.text())))
                widget.clicked.connect(
                    lambda checked, button=widget: self._clicked(button, checked))
        elif isinstance(widget, QComboBox):
            if not self._marked(widget):
                widget.activated.connect(lambda index, combo=widget: self._chosen(combo, index))
        elif isinstance(widget, QTabBar):
            if not self._marked(widget):
                widget.tabBarClicked.connect(lambda index, tabs=widget: self._tab(tabs, index))
        elif isinstance(widget, QAbstractItemView):
            if not self._marked(widget):
                widget.doubleClicked.connect(lambda index, view=widget: self._double(view, index))

    def _connect_action(self, action):
        if action is None or action.isSeparator() or action.menu() is not None:
            return
        if not self._marked(action):
            action.triggered.connect(lambda checked, act=action: self._triggered(act, checked))

    @staticmethod
    def _clicked(button, checked):
        text = button.property(_PRESSED)
        button.setProperty(_PRESSED, None)
        fields = {**_window(button), "widget": type(button).__name__, **_name(button),
                  "text": text or _text(button.text()) or button.toolTip()[:80]}
        if button.isCheckable():
            fields["checked"] = checked
        activity.record("click", **fields)

    @staticmethod
    def _triggered(action, checked):
        fields = {"text": _text(action.text()) or action.toolTip()[:80], **_name(action)}
        parent = action.parent()
        if parent is not None and parent.isWidgetType():
            fields.update(_window(parent))
        if action.isCheckable():
            fields["checked"] = checked
        activity.record("action", **fields)

    @staticmethod
    def _chosen(combo, index):
        activity.record("choice", **_window(combo), **_name(combo),
                        text=combo.itemText(index), index=index)

    @staticmethod
    def _tab(tabs, index):
        if index >= 0:
            activity.record("tab", **_window(tabs), text=_text(tabs.tabText(index)))

    @staticmethod
    def _double(view, index):
        activity.record("double_click", **_window(view), widget=type(view).__name__,
                        **_name(view), row=index.row(), column=index.column())

```

`hermes/ui/garbage.py`:

```py
"""Python's garbage collector, run in the GUI thread only.

Left automatic, the collector runs in whatever thread allocates when a
threshold is crossed, often a hook or Frida thread. Qt objects in the cycles
it frees are then deleted by PySide6 later in the GUI thread, and with
widgets that can crash the interpreter (a widget deleted twice). Here the
automatic collector is off and a timer in the GUI thread collects instead,
by the same thresholds.
"""

import gc

from PySide6.QtCore import QObject, QTimer  # pylint: disable=import-error,no-name-in-module

INTERVAL_MS = 500


class GarbageCollector(QObject):
    """Collects garbage in the thread it lives in; see the module docstring."""

    def __init__(self, parent=None, interval_ms=INTERVAL_MS):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self._timer = QTimer(self)
        self._timer.setInterval(interval_ms)
        self._timer.timeout.connect(self.check)
        self._was_enabled = None

    def start(self):
        self._was_enabled = gc.isenabled()
        gc.disable()
        self._timer.start()

    def stop(self):
        """Hand collecting back to Python, if it collected before ``start``."""
        self._timer.stop()
        if self._was_enabled:
            gc.enable()

    @staticmethod
    def check():
        """Collect the oldest generation whose count is over its threshold."""
        counts = gc.get_count()
        thresholds = gc.get_threshold()
        if counts[0] <= thresholds[0]:
            return
        generation = 0
        for older in (1, 2):
            if thresholds[older] and counts[older] > thresholds[older]:
                generation = older
        gc.collect(generation)

```

`hermes/ui/localization.py`:

```py
"""Load the UI translations for the selected language."""

import json
import locale
import os
from pathlib import Path


_SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES = {"de", "en"}
_CATALOG_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "localization"


def language_code(language: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Resolve a language to one of the UI's supported short codes."""
    selected_language = language or os.environ.get("HERMES_LANGUAGE")
    if not selected_language:
        selected_language = locale.getlocale()[0] or "en"

    code = selected_language.replace("-", "_").split("_", maxsplit=1)[0].lower()
    if code not in _SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES:
        code = "en"
    return code


def load_translations(language: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Load a catalog, preferring an explicit choice over the system locale."""
    code = language_code(language)

    catalog_path = _CATALOG_DIR / f"{code}.json"
    return json.loads(catalog_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
```

`hermes/ui/localization/de.json`:

```json
{
  "app.window_title": "Hermes Hook",
```

`hermes/ui/main_window.py`:

```py
"""hermes-hook – Main Window: application main UI (PySide6)."""

import itertools
import platform
import sys
import time
from dataclasses import dataclass

# How often to check whether the attached process is still running.
PROCESS_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS = 1000
# A game that ends this long after Hermes last used debug registers in it may
# have detected them (anti-debug code, e.g. Arxan in Dark Souls III, checks
# them every few seconds).
DEBUG_REGISTER_CRASH_WINDOW_S = 30
# How long closing the window waits for the Frida workers of the C# windows
# (trace, method monitor) to remove their interceptors before it goes on;
# the shutdown dialog waits for what still runs then.
CLOSING_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS = 3_000

# Upper bound for joining a write monitor from the GUI thread.
WRITE_WATCH_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS = 3000
# Scan results beyond this many rows are kept but not shown in the table.
RESULT_DISPLAY_LIMIT = 1000

# The app icon (window and taskbar, see hermes.main; toolbar)
ICON_PATH = Path(__file__).parent / "resources" / "favicon.svg"
# Its size next to the name in the toolbar
BRAND_ICON_SIZE = 22


class GadgetProgressDialog(QProgressDialog):
    """Progress dialog updated by the gadget download worker."""

    @Slot(int, int)
    def set_download_progress(self, received, total):
        if total <= 0:
            self.setRange(0, 0)
            return
        self.setRange(0, total)
        self.setValue(min(received, total))


def _platform_text():
    """The system Hermes runs on for the status bar, e.g. ``Windows x86-64``."""
    system = "Windows" if sys.platform == "win32" else "Linux"
    machine = platform.machine()
    if machine.lower() in ("x86_64", "amd64"):
        machine = "x86-64"
    return f"{system} {machine}"


def _unless_dropped(worker, slot):
    """``slot``, but deaf to ``worker`` once ``_drop`` let it go.

    Disconnecting is not enough: PySide6 still delivers the signals a worker
    queued before.
    """
    def call(*args):
        if not getattr(worker, "hermes_dropped", False):
            slot(*args)
    return call


def _drop(worker):
    """Let the slots connected through ``_unless_dropped`` ignore ``worker``."""
    worker.hermes_dropped = True


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ScanRequest:
    """Inputs required to start an initial or follow-up scan."""

    pid: int | None
    value_type: str
    scan_mode: str
    value: str
    value2: str = ""
    previous_results: ScanResults | MemorySnapshot | None = None
    aligned: bool = True
    tolerance: str = ""
    float_rounding: str = "exact"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dialog: edit value
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class ValueInputDialog(QDialog):
    # Dialogs expose behavior through Qt signals rather than public methods.
    # pylint: disable=too-few-public-methods
    """Simple dialog for entering a new value for a tracked address."""

    def __init__(self, address: str, current_value: str, value_type: str,
                 parent=None, translations=None):
        """Initialize the dialog and build its value editor."""
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.translations = translations or load_translations()
        self.setWindowTitle(self.translations["value_dialog.title"])
        self.setFixedSize(340, 160)
        self.new_value = None
        self._build_ui(address, current_value, value_type)

    def _build_ui(self, address, current, vtype):
        """Build the address details, input field, and dialog buttons."""
        layout = QVBoxLayout(self)
        layout.setSpacing(10)

        info = QLabel(
            f"{self.translations['value_dialog.address']}: "
            f"<span style='color:{theme_color('success')}'>{address}</span>"
            f"  &nbsp;{self.translations['value_dialog.type']}: "
            f"<span style='color:{theme_color('orange')}'>{vtype}</span>"
        )
        info.setTextFormat(Qt.TextFormat.RichText)
        layout.addWidget(info)

        self.input = QLineEdit(current)
        self.input.selectAll()
        self.input.setPlaceholderText(self.translations["value_dialog.placeholder"])
        layout.addWidget(self.input)

        layout.addLayout(dialog_button_row(
            self.translations, "button.write", self._accept, self.reject
        ))

    def _accept(self):
        """Store the entered value and accept the dialog."""
        self.new_value = self.input.text().strip()
        self.accept()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dialog: add an address by hand
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
class AddressInputDialog(QDialog):
    # Dialogs expose behavior through Qt signals rather than public methods.
    # pylint: disable=too-few-public-methods
    """Dialog for putting an address on the address list by hand.

    ``parse(text)`` turns the entered address into a number or raises
    ValueError; it also accepts ``module+0x…``.
    """

    def __init__(self, parse, value_type, parent=None, translations=None):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self.translations = translations or load_translations()
        self.setWindowTitle(self.translations["address_dialog.title"])
        self.setMinimumWidth(420)
        self._parse = parse
        # (description, address, value type) once accepted
        self.result_entry = None
        self._build_ui(value_type)

    def _build_ui(self, value_type):
        layout = QVBoxLayout(self)
        layout.setSpacing(10)
        form = QFormLayout()
        self.address_input = QLineEdit()
        self.address_input.setPlaceholderText(
            self.translations["address_dialog.address_placeholder"])
        form.addRow(self.translations["address_table.address"], self.address_input)
        self.type_combo = QComboBox()
        for name in VALUE_TYPES:
            self.type_combo.addItem(name, name)
        self.type_combo.setCurrentIndex(max(self.type_combo.findData(value_type), 0))
        form.addRow(self.translations["address_table.type"], self.type_combo)
        self.description_input = QLineEdit(self.translations["address_table.new_address"])
        form.addRow(self.translations["address_table.description"], self.description_input)
        layout.addLayout(form)

        self.error_label = QLabel()
        self.error_label.setStyleSheet(f"color: {theme_color('danger')};")
        self.error_label.setWordWrap(True)
        self.error_label.hide()
        layout.addWidget(self.error_label)

        layout.addLayout(dialog_button_row(
            self.translations, "button.add", self._accept, self.reject
        ))

    def _accept(self):
        try:
            address = self._parse(self.address_input.text())
        except UnknownModuleError as error:
            self.error_label.setText(
                self.translations["address_dialog.unknown_module"].format(module=error.module))
            self.error_label.show()
            self.address_input.setFocus()
            return
        except ValueError:
            self.error_label.setText(self.translations["address_dialog.invalid"])
            self.error_label.show()
            self.address_input.setFocus()
            return
        description = (self.description_input.text().strip()
                       or self.translations["address_table.new_address"])
        self.result_entry = (description, address, self.type_combo.currentData())
        self.accept()

            material_icon("delete_sweep"), self.translations["menu.delete_entries"])
        self.act_delete_entries.setToolTip(self.translations["menu.delete_entries_tooltip"])
        self.act_delete_entries.triggered.connect(self._open_delete_entries)
        self.act_vacuum = file_menu.addAction(
            material_icon("compress"), self.translations["menu.vacuum"])
        self.act_vacuum.setToolTip(self.translations["menu.vacuum_tooltip"])

        file_menu.addSeparator()
        self.act_check_gadget = file_menu.addAction(
            material_icon("refresh"), self.translations["menu.check_gadget"])

        settings_menu = menu_bar.addMenu(self.translations["menu.settings"])
        settings_menu.setToolTipsVisible(True)
        self.act_settings = settings_menu.addAction(
            material_icon("settings"), self.translations["menu.general_settings"])
        self.act_settings.setToolTip(self.translations["menu.general_settings_tooltip"])
        self.act_settings.triggered.connect(self._open_settings)

            group.addAction(action)
            self._backend_actions[backend] = action
```
